inventories.subsystem: App shell, windowing, input, menus, HUD, settings, persistence, packaging (Marvin Simulator macOS, branch codex/mos-aster-racing-city @1c8bb11)
inventories.overview:
The app is a single-window AppKit program. main.swift creates NSApplication.shared (activation policy .regular), installs AppController (NSApplicationDelegate, NSWindowDelegate, NSToolbarDelegate), and calls app.run(). applicationDidFinishLaunching (App.swift:96-185) loads the four robot models from Bundle.main.resourceURL synchronously. If a load fails, it shows a modal NSAlert and terminates. It then builds a 1280x820-pt window (minimum 900x640, .fullSizeContentView, centred) and makes its content view a SimulatorView, which subclasses SCNView (MSAA 4x, 60 fps, rendersContinuously). An NSToolbar holds 5 SF-Symbol items, and a custom NSMenu bar is installed.

All UI is AppKit NSView overlays added as subviews of the SCNView and pinned to window.contentLayoutGuide, so the 3D viewport never resizes when chrome changes. The overlays are: HUDView (sandbox), RaceHUD (race), MainMenuView (opaque menu with native NSTextField and NSButton plus a second SCNView 'portrait' stage), FrameRateHUD, and LevelLoadingView. The HUDs are immediate-mode Quartz drawing (NSBezierPath plus NSString.draw with the SF Pro / SF Mono system fonts), invalidated every tick and composited by Core Animation over the Metal layer.

Timing: a Foundation Timer at 1/60 s on the main run loop (.common modes) calls tick(). tick() reads ProcessInfo.systemUptime, clamps the simulation dt to 0.1 s, and uses the unclamped wall delta for the race clock. SceneKit renders independently on its own thread at preferredFramesPerSecond=60. Its SCNSceneRendererDelegate (TownFrameMeter) only measures render cadence for the FPS HUD. An optional macOS 14 CADisplayLink path exists behind diagnostic flags.

The simulation advances only when the app is active, the window occlusionState contains .visible, and the game is not paused. Losing focus, losing key status, miniaturising or becoming occluded clears held keys and stops audio. lastTime is reset on reactivation so no time is caught up.

Input is raw NSEvent keyCodes, i.e. physical mac virtual keys. A held-key set maps to DriveInput (throttle, turn, head yaw/pitch, boost=Shift, brake=Space). One-shot commands are G (gate), C (camera), P/Esc (pause), H (centre head) and '/' or '?' (help). Command-key shortcuts go to the menu bar: Cmd-M, Cmd-R, Cmd-P, Cmd-1, Cmd-Q. Mouse drag orbits the camera and the scroll wheel zooms. There is no gamepad support.

The main menu offers Sandbox, Dirt Track, Settings and Quit. Hidden letter keys choose the character: B, R, W, M. Settings are 5 booleans stored in UserDefaults with inverted keys. A 'Mute race sound' menu item also persists.

Choosing Dirt Track shows a loading screen while DirtWorld is built on a GCD background queue. Progress is posted to the main thread and forced monotonic. The scene is then pre-compiled with SCNView.prepare before it is revealed.

Best scores are stored as a JSON array of {date, laps[3]}, top 10, written with Data.write(.atomic) to ~/Library/Application Support/Marvin Simulator/motocross-v4-scores.json.

The dock icon switches between AppIconLight.icns and AppIconDark.icns by observing NSApp.effectiveAppearance.

Packaging: build-app.sh runs the Python asset exporters and `swift build`. It assembles '.build/Marvin Simulator.app' by copying Info.plist, the binary and the Resources folders, then ad-hoc codesigns it. 'Launch Marvin.command' wraps this in a Python TUI launcher.

The same binary also hosts about 30 smoke-test and benchmark modes chosen by command-line flag. They synthesise NSEvents, take SCNView snapshots and cacheDisplay captures, write JSON reports, and exit with a status code.

platform_dependencies.purpose: Process bootstrap, run loop, lifecycle, and active/inactive gating of the simulation and audio. Quits when the last window closes.
platform_dependencies.windows_options: Win32 wWinMain plus a PeekMessage game loop (WM_ACTIVATEAPP, WM_CLOSE/WM_DESTROY -> PostQuitMessage); SDL3 (SDL_AppInit/SDL_AppIterate/SDL_AppEvent, SDL_EVENT_WINDOW_FOCUS_LOST/GAINED, SDL_EVENT_QUIT); GLFW (glfwSetWindowFocusCallback); engine-native lifecycle (Unity OnApplicationFocus/OnApplicationPause + Application.runInBackground=false; Unreal FCoreDelegates::ApplicationWillDeactivateDelegate/HasReactivated; Godot NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT/IN). platform_dependencies.fidelity_risk: Models (Marvin alone is 695k triangles) load synchronously before the window appears (App.swift:101-111). On Windows a message pump blocked for more than 5 s triggers the 'Not Responding' ghost window. Windows also restricts foreground activation, so the window may not come to the front at launch.

platform_dependencies.purpose: The single game window. Titles change per mode. The 3D view extends under the title bar and toolbar (fullSizeContentView) while HUD overlays sit in the safe content area. Hiding or showing the toolbar must not change the window frame or the renderer viewport.
platform_dependencies.windows_options: CreateWindowExW (WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW), with WM_GETMINMAXINFO for the 900x640 DIP minimum scaled by GetDpiForWindow and AdjustWindowRectExForDpi for the 1280x820 client size. Centre via MonitorFromWindow/GetMonitorInfo. Titles via SetWindowTextW. To extend content under a translucent caption: DwmExtendFrameIntoClientArea + DWMWA_SYSTEMBACKDROP_TYPE (Mica/Acrylic, Win11 22H2+) and custom WM_NCCALCSIZE/WM_NCHITTEST. Alternatives: SDL3 SDL_CreateWindow + SDL_SetWindowMinimumSize + SDL_SetWindowTitle; WinUI 3 Window + SwapChainPanel; engine window settings (Unity resizable window, Screen.SetResolution; Unreal UGameUserSettings; Godot DisplayServer.window_set_min_size).
platform_dependencies.fidelity_risk: On macOS the scene renders blurred under the translucent unified title bar and toolbar; a standard Windows caption is opaque. macOS points (integer 2x) become DIPs at fractional 125/150/175% scaling, which changes hairlines and text rasterisation. During a resize or move drag (WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE modal loop) a Windows game loop stalls, whereas the macOS Timer in .common modes keeps ticking. The viewport smoke test requires zero drift (<0.01 px) when chrome toggles.

platform_dependencies.purpose: App menu: 'About Marvin Simulator', 'Quit Marvin Simulator' (Cmd-Q). 'Simulation' menu: Main Menu (Cmd-M), Reset playground (Cmd-R), Pause / resume (Cmd-P), Change camera (Cmd-1), and 'Mute race sound' (checkmark toggle persisted to UserDefaults 'raceSoundMuted', no shortcut). platform_dependencies.windows_options: Win32 HMENU menu bar (CreateMenu/AppendMenuW, CheckMenuItem MF_CHECKED) plus an accelerator table mapping Ctrl+M/R/P/1 and Alt+F4 (optionally Ctrl+Q). platform_dependencies.fidelity_risk: A Win32 menu bar occupies client-area height under the caption, unlike the mac global menu bar. Alt or F10 puts Windows into menu mode (WM_SYSKEYDOWN/SC_KEYMENU), after which WASD navigates menus during gameplay; this must be suppressed. All on-screen hint strings contain the glyph '⌘R' and must become 'Ctrl+R'.

platform_dependencies.purpose: Gameplay uses physical key codes in a held set: 0 A, 1 S, 2 D, 13 W, 12 Q, 14 E, 15 R, 3 F, 49 Space, 123-126 arrows, 56 Shift (any shift via flagsChanged). One-shot commands fire on non-repeat keyDown: 5 G (gate), 8 C (camera), 35 P and 53 Esc (pause), 4 H (centre head), 44 '/' or '?' (help). Command-modified keys pass to super for menu equivalents. Main menu: arrows (124/125 next, 123/126 previous), Return 36 / keypad Enter 76 / Space 49 activate (non-repeat), Esc 53 leaves Settings. Character letters m/b/r/w come from characters (layout-dependent) and are ignored with Control or Option held. The loading view swallows keys. Losing first responder clears input.
platform_dependencies.windows_options: WM_KEYDOWN/WM_KEYUP using the hardware scancode (lParam bits 16-23 plus the extended bit 24) to keep positional WASD on AZERTY/QWERTZ; repeat from lParam bit 30. WM_CHAR or ToUnicodeEx for the layout-dependent menu letters. Raw Input (RIM_TYPEKEYBOARD); SDL3 SDL_EVENT_KEY_DOWN/UP with SDL_Scancode (physical, equivalent to kVK codes) and event.repeat, plus SDL_EVENT_TEXT_INPUT or keycodes for letters. GameInput. Engines: Unity Input System Key (physical layout), Unreal FKey/EKeys, Godot InputEventKey.physical_keycode.
platform_dependencies.fidelity_risk: Cmd must map to Ctrl. Pressing Shift five times triggers the Windows Sticky Keys prompt, and Shift is boost (games disable it via SystemParametersInfo SPI_SETSTICKYKEYS while focused). The Windows key opens Start. IME composition can swallow keys. Space activates focused Win32 buttons. macOS delivers flagsChanged for Shift, whereas Windows sends VK_SHIFT/VK_LSHIFT/VK_RSHIFT keydowns with repeats. Input must be cleared on WM_KILLFOCUS to reproduce resignFirstResponder.

platform_dependencies.purpose: Orbit camera: yaw += dx*0.008, pitch = clamp(pitch + dy*0.008, 0.15, 1.35), switching to ORBIT mode. Zoom: distance = clamp(d + scrollingDeltaY*0.035, 1.6, 9). Allowed only in Sandbox or Dirt Track, not during the intro flight and not after the race finishes; also allowed while paused. Menu portrait: horizontal drag rotates the model by 0.01 rad per point.
platform_dependencies.windows_options: WM_MOUSEMOVE with SetCapture/ReleaseCapture (left and right button), WM_MOUSEWHEEL (WHEEL_DELTA=120 per notch; precision touchpads send smaller fractional deltas), WM_POINTER* messages, Raw Input mouse deltas. SDL3 SDL_EVENT_MOUSE_MOTION xrel/yrel and SDL_EVENT_MOUSE_WHEEL y (float, precise). Engine input axes.
platform_dependencies.fidelity_risk: The coefficients are tuned to macOS pointer acceleration and to scrollingDeltaY, which is pixel-precise on trackpads, line-based on wheels, and honours natural-scrolling direction. Wheel and touchpad deltas on Windows need calibration and a sign decision, or zoom and orbit speed will feel different.

platform_dependencies.where: SimulatorView.swift:42-139 (HUDView); RaceHUD.swift:20-209; RaceNavigationMap.swift:45-85; FrameRateHUD.swift:34-44; LevelLoading.swift:3-12; App.swift:435, 446, 709-716
platform_dependencies.purpose: All in-game HUDs: sandbox cards, minimap and help; race standings, scores, map, countdown, pause, storm warning, results and departure panels; FPS counter; loading progress bar. They are redrawn by CPU rasterisation into layer backing stores at roughly 60 Hz and composited over the Metal layer by Core Animation.
platform_dependencies.windows_options: Direct2D 1.1 ID2D1DeviceContext targeting the DXGI back buffer (or an overlay surface) with DirectWrite. This is the closest Quartz/CoreText analogue: rounded rectangles, ellipses, path geometries, ID2D1StrokeStyle with dashes and round joins, layers and clips, transforms. Skia (SkCanvas on D3D12/Vulkan/GL, near-identical geometric AA semantics). NanoVG. Dear ImGui ImDrawList (adequate shapes, different text). RmlUi / NoesisGUI / Ultralight. Engine UI: Godot CanvasItem draw_* + draw_string (very close API shape), Unity UI Toolkit Painter2D + TextCore, Unreal Slate OnPaint (FSlateDrawElement MakeBox/MakeLines/MakeText) or UMG.
platform_dependencies.fidelity_risk: Pixel parity is hard. Text antialiasing differs (macOS grayscale with subpixel positioning versus ClearType or grayscale DirectWrite). Corner shapes, stroke alignment and 1-pt hairline rules differ. NSColor sRGB versus 'calibrated' (generic) RGB leads to small colour shifts. Core Animation composites in sRGB-encoded space; an engine compositing UI in a linear or HDR buffer would change translucent panel blending (panels use alpha 0.9 / 0.94 / 0.42). Panel widths are computed from measured text, so any font-metric change resizes panels.

platform_dependencies.purpose: All UI typography at weights regular, medium, semibold and bold, sizes 9-80 pt. 3D beacon numerals in the sandbox. Condensed sign lettering in town.
platform_dependencies.windows_options: Bundle OFL/Apache fonts: Inter or Inter Display (closest SF Pro metrics), JetBrains Mono / IBM Plex Mono / Roboto Mono / Fira Mono (SF Mono stand-ins), Barlow Semi Condensed / Roboto Condensed / Archivo Narrow (Avenir Next Condensed). Or Windows system fonts with nothing shipped: Segoe UI Variable, Cascadia Mono, Consolas. Use the OpenType 'tnum' feature for monospacedDigit. For SCNText glyph outlines: DirectWrite IDWriteFontFace::GetGlyphRunOutline to an ID2D1SimplifiedGeometrySink, or FreeType FT_Outline_Decompose, then triangulate (earcut / libtess2) at an equivalent flatness of 0.2.
platform_dependencies.fidelity_risk: Apple's SF Pro, SF Mono and Avenir Next licences do not permit redistribution or use on Windows, so 'same graphics' for text is impossible verbatim. Every glyph shape and width changes, the auto-sized HUD panels and menu layout shift, and wrapping or clipping in fixed rects (e.g. 'Race finished' 30 pt bold in w-48) may break.

platform_dependencies.framework: SceneKit / Metal (the rendering readers cover the internals)
platform_dependencies.purpose: Main viewport (4x MSAA in Sandbox, 2x in Dirt Track) and a separate continuously rendered portrait viewport for the menu. Pre-compiles materials and uploads geometry before the race is revealed. Render-callback cadence feeds the FPS HUD. Snapshots feed tests.
platform_dependencies.windows_options: An engine or custom renderer with two viewports (a main swapchain plus a render-to-texture or second swapchain for the portrait). PSO/shader warm-up to replace prepare(): D3D12 pipeline libraries / PSO cache, Vulkan VkPipelineCache, Unity ShaderVariantCollection.WarmUp / PSO tracing, Unreal PSO precaching, Godot ubershaders and shader baker. Frame callbacks map to engine post-render hooks. Back-buffer readback for snapshots.
platform_dependencies.fidelity_risk: The main view keeps rendering world.scene behind the opaque menu, which wastes GPU time but is invisible. The portrait uses its own lighting and shadow setup (see fidelity spec). HUD overlays are excluded from SCNView.snapshot, and the tests rely on that split.

platform_dependencies.api: Foundation Timer(timeInterval:1/60) added to RunLoop.main in .common modes; ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime; NSView.displayLink(target:selector:) + CADisplayLink.preferredFrameRateRange(60,60,60) (macOS 14+, diagnostic only)
platform_dependencies.purpose: Simulation clock and update driver (main thread, 60 Hz), decoupled from SceneKit's render thread. The display-link path is selected only by --display-link-updates, --benchmark-display-link or --display-link-lifecycle-check (and not when --benchmark-timer is given).
platform_dependencies.windows_options: QueryPerformanceCounter/QueryPerformanceFrequency (or std::chrono::steady_clock) for the clock. Run updates from the game loop at render cadence with the same variable-dt clamp, or on a high-resolution waitable timer (CreateWaitableTimerExW with CREATE_WAITABLE_TIMER_HIGH_RESOLUTION, Win10 1803+). SetTimer/WM_TIMER is about 15.6 ms granular (unless timeBeginPeriod(1)) and unsuitable. Pace to vblank with a DXGI flip-model swapchain, Present(1) and the frame-latency waitable object (IDXGISwapChain2::GetFrameLatencyWaitableObject), or DwmFlush. Engines: Unity Application.targetFrameRate=60 + QualitySettings.vSyncCount; Unreal t.MaxFPS 60 / bUseFixedFrameRate; Godot Engine.max_fps=60.
platform_dependencies.fidelity_risk: preferredFramesPerSecond=60 caps rendering at 60 even on 120 Hz ProMotion; Windows 144/165 Hz monitors need an explicit cap. The update/render beat pattern of a 60 Hz main-thread Timer against a separate 60 Hz render thread is not reproduced by a single-threaded loop; the measured smoothness differs slightly. Windows modal loops (resize, move, menu) stop the loop unless rendering continues from WM_TIMER or another thread.

platform_dependencies.purpose: Freeze race and simulation time and stop audio when the window is hidden, covered or minimised. Clear input on resign-key. Reset lastTime so there is no catch-up. Reset FPS samples.
platform_dependencies.windows_options: WM_SIZE SIZE_MINIMIZED/SIZE_RESTORED, IsIconic, WM_ACTIVATE/WM_KILLFOCUS. DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED from Present, or IDXGIFactory::RegisterOcclusionStatusWindow. Windows cannot reliably detect a windowed app being covered (DXGI occlusion mainly covers minimised or locked states). Behaviour on partial or total coverage will differ unless the rule is restated as pause on minimise or inactive.

platform_dependencies.purpose: The Dock icon follows the system light or dark appearance live. Finder and pre-launch show the light .icns.
platform_dependencies.windows_options: Embed the light .ico as the exe icon resource (the Finder-fallback analogue). At runtime read HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize AppsUseLightTheme / SystemUsesLightTheme, listen for WM_SETTINGCHANGE with lParam 'ImmersiveColorSet' or WinRT UISettings.ColorValuesChanged, and swap WM_SETICON (ICON_BIG/ICON_SMALL) between the light and dark .ico. platform_dependencies.fidelity_risk: Pinned taskbar shortcuts and Explorer use the static exe or shortcut icon, so the dark icon appears only while running and only if unpinned. The taskbar colour follows SystemUsesLightTheme, not AppsUseLightTheme. A 16-1024 px .icns needs a .ico counterpart (16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 256).

Items in order: Main Menu ('house'), flexible space, Camera ('video'), Pause ('pause.fill'; becomes 'Resume' with 'play.fill' while paused), Reset ('arrow.counterclockwise'), Controls ('keyboard'). Display mode icon+label; tooltip equals the label. Visible only in Sandbox and Dirt Track gameplay. Hidden on the main menu, during loading, and while the post-race 'escape' departure is active (setRaceControlsHidden also hides the race HUD and FPS HUD).

App menu: About Marvin Simulator; separator; Quit Marvin Simulator (Cmd-Q). Simulation menu: Main Menu (Cmd-M), Reset playground (Cmd-R), Pause / resume (Cmd-P), Change camera (Cmd-1), Mute race sound (checkmark, persisted as 'raceSoundMuted'; muting stops audio immediately).

Held keys: W/Up = throttle +1; S/Down = -1; D/Right = turn +1; A/Left = turn -1; E = headYaw +1; Q = -1; R = headPitch +1; F = -1; Shift (either side) = boost; Space = brake. throttle = max(W,Up) - max(S,Down) (digital, no analog). One-shot keys on non-repeat keydown: G toggles the city gate (Dirt Track only, hidden); C cycles camera; P or Esc toggles pause; H centres the head; '/' or '?' (kVK_ANSI_Slash) toggles the help panel (not persisted). Any Command-modified key goes to the menu bar instead of gameplay. Key repeat is ignored for commands. Focus loss, resign-key, pause, reset or a camera cut clear all held keys; in Sandbox that also zeroes velocity (simulation.stop()), while in Dirt Track momentum is kept.

Left or right drag sets camera mode ORBIT, orbitYaw += deltaX*0.008 and orbitPitch = clamp(orbitPitch + deltaY*0.008, 0.15, 1.35). Scroll sets cameraDistance = clamp(distance + scrollingDeltaY*0.035, 1.6, 9). Both are allowed only when inSandbox (Sandbox or Dirt Track), with no intro flight running and the race camera not locked (post-finish). Paused does not block them. A click focuses the 3D view. HUD overlays are click-through (hitTest nil).

Modes: 0 FOLLOW, 1 ORBIT, 2 OVERVIEW. Defaults: mode 1, yaw 0.65, pitch 0.5, distance 3.5. Dirt reset: mode 0, distance 4.5. Follow: angle = heading + pi (+0.45 in Sandbox); elevation 0.30 (Dirt) or 0.48 (Sandbox); look-ahead 1.5 in Dirt follow mode; target = (x + sin(h)*la, groundY + 0.35, z + cos(h)*la); eye = (x + sin(a)cos(e)d, groundY + 0.4 + sin(e)d, z + cos(a)cos(e)d); eye smoothing mix = 1 - exp(-7.67 dt). Overview: Dirt course eye (0,38,-33) aiming at the origin; Sandbox (0,11.7,-10); outside the course region the eye is target + (0,38,-33) aiming at the target; smoothing is OverviewMotion, critically damped with omega 8 and dt clamped to 0.1. Intro flight 3.2 s: t = clamp((intro-0.35)/(3.2-0.35)), smootherstep 6t^5-15t^4+10t^3 from (0,38,-33) to the chase pose, aim lerped from the origin. Outro reverses this from the current pose to (0,38,-33), aim from 4.5 units in front to the origin. After the finish the camera locks to (0,38,-33) looking at the origin. Dirt boom collision against town: boom fraction shrinks instantly and regrows at 1 - exp(-3.5 dt); within 1.5 units of the pivot the aim is raised toward chassis height + 0.45. The overview eye stays at least 0.18 above terrain. Up vector is (0,1,0) and localFront (0,0,-1). HUD camera labels: FOLLOW, ORBIT, OVERVIEW. Main-view FOV: World.swift camera fieldOfView 48 (SceneKit default vertical projection direction), zNear 0.02, zFar 80 (Sandbox) or 250 (Dirt).

'Connecting residents to their homes'); 0.49 'Planning routes through town'; 0.495 'Preparing the sand and racecourse'; 0.50-0.84 'Building the dunes'; 0.86 'Building track walls and gate'; 0.90 'Preparing robots and race'; 0.93 'Getting ready to race' (SCNView.prepare); 1.0 'Ready'. The world is built on a background queue the first time only; later entries reuse the cached DirtWorld and skip the build stages. Keys are swallowed and the toolbar hidden. The first frame is rendered via snapshot() before the reveal. On failure the app returns to the menu with an alert.

The update tick is a 60 Hz main-thread Timer. dt = min(wall delta, 0.1) drives the simulation; raceDelta = the unclamped wall delta drives the race timer. Smoke modes use a fixed 1/60 for both. The simulation advances only if (app active AND window occlusionState is visible AND not paused) or a smoke mode is running. While not advancing, world effects update with dt 0 but the camera keeps smoothing. lastTime is reset on activation, occlusion change, deminiaturise, reveal and load completion, so time is never caught up. Rendering is separate: SceneKit at 60 fps. Pause (P, Esc, toolbar, Cmd-P) toggles simulation.paused, clears input, stops audio and relabels the toolbar. Resign-active clears input and stops audio. Countdown and driving start only after the 3.2 s intro. The race clock excludes countdown, pause and inactivity.

Materials via material(): lightingModel .physicallyBased, diffuse sRGB hex, metalness 0, roughness 0.6 by default, double-sided. Chamfered SCNBox geometry: plinth 12.5x0.3x10.5 (r 0.14, 0x927455, roughness 0.95), soil backing 12x0.05x10 (r 0.04, 0xb49470, roughness 0.98), four walls 0.16x0.36 (0xa5b9ad, r 0.04), five obstacles (alternating 0x96b4a7 / 0xd2b59a, r 0.07), dock inlay 1.35x0.001x1.25 (0xb7cdc0) with two teal 0x2b8e7f stripes. The floor surface is an SCNShape from an even-odd NSBezierPath (12x10 rectangle minus 128-segment circles), rebuilt whenever checkpoints change, plus 128-segment SCNCylinder discs (h 0.025). The grid is lines 0.009 wide x 0.005 high (0xa48766, roughness 0.98) at integer x in -5..5 and z in -4..4, split around the rings and dock. Five FloorGroove V-rings: depth 0.012, 2 bands x 128 segments, material 0x70583f, roughness 0.95. Ring colours: done 0x2b8e7f, active 0xc38b41, pending 0x70583f. The active ring pulses its emission at glow = 0.18 + 0.06*(1 + sin(2t)), colour sRGB (glow, 0.55 glow, 0.12 glow). Labels are SCNText digits 1-5 in SF Mono semibold (size 1, flatness 0.2, extrusion 0), scaled to 0.36 height, laid flat at y 0.0008, yawed by CourseRoute.labelYaw, colour 0x4e756a. Markers and lines do not cast shadows.

fidelity_spec.feature: Race lifecycle hooks owned by the shell
fidelity_spec.parameters: Dirt entry: load scores, reset with a random grid shuffle (SystemRandomNumberGenerator), random daylight, a 10% storm draw (sets the window title), intro 0, camera snap. Cmd-R repeats all of this. The score is recorded once when the player finishes. After the finish: outro flight, camera locked, autopilot. setRaceControlsHidden(true) during the departure hides the race HUD, FPS readout and toolbar without resizing the window. Audio is created lazily on first Dirt entry and is audible only when not muted, racing, advancing and the intro has ended.

Path: ~/Library/Application Support/Marvin Simulator/motocross-v4-scores.json (v2 and v3 files are left untouched); smoke runs use <dir>/test-scores.json. Format: compact JSON array of {"date": <Double, seconds since 2001-01-01 UTC>, "laps": [Double, Double, Double]}, without guaranteed key order. Valid means exactly 3 finite laps, each > 0. Stored ranked ascending by total, at most 10. Written atomically (Data.write .atomic, after createDirectory). Load errors set scoreLoadFailed: the existing file is preserved, never overwritten, and the HUD shows 'Could not load scores; file preserved' and 'High scores unavailable'. A save error shows 'Could not save score'. The HUD displays the top 5.

AppIconLight.icns and AppIconDark.icns (16-512 @1x and @2x), plus 1024 px PNG and SVG. Rounded tile: rect 64..960 in a 1024 canvas, rx 196, vertical gradient. Light: #f8f7f2 to #e9e8e1, glyph #202521, edge #ffffff. Dark: #303631 to #1b211d, glyph #f3f3e9, edge #596259. Edge stroke 3 px at opacity 0.65. Entire symbol at translate(171,160) scale 22. The runtime Dock icon switches on effectiveAppearance (aqua or darkAqua); Info.plist's static fallback is light.

color(hex) = NSColor(srgbRed:green:blue:alpha:), sRGB, used for UI and materials. FrameRateHUD, the LoadingProgressBar and LevelLoadingView use NSColor(calibratedRed:/calibratedWhite:), i.e. generic RGB or gray, which differ slightly from sRGB.

inventories.portable_logic:
Reusable verbatim or nearly verbatim (counts approximate):
1) SimulationCore, 2,333 lines in 20 files, Foundation + Apple `simd`. It holds the simulation, DriveInput, DirtRace/DirtScore/DirtScores (JSON persistence), DirtStandings, RaceMapRegion and OverviewMotion (camera damping), TownFootprint, CourseLayout/CourseRoute and RacePerformance. It is portable to Swift on Windows with a roughly 100-line `simd` shim (about 85 simd_* call sites). Ported to C++ or C# it needs a full rewrite but no redesign.
2) Tests/SimulationCoreTests ('SimulationChecks'), 1,671 lines. This is a custom @main harness with no XCTest, using Foundation + simd + SimulationCore. It is portable with the same shim, and includes the score save/load round trip.
3) Shell logic in App.swift that is pure math or state, about 250 lines. Camera rig updateCamera, about 90 lines on SCNVector3, which can become SIMD3<Double>. advanceRaceFrame gating, about 25. The tick ordering and advancing rule, about 40. Reset with grid shuffle, storm draw and title, about 30. Pause, help and cycle-camera state, about 20. recordRaceScore, about 8. The smootherstep intro and outro.
4) Input mapping, about 15 lines (SimulatorView.driveInput plus the command switch). It needs only a keycode-to-scancode table.
5) Main-menu state machine and idle animation, about 100 lines (MainMenu.refresh/activate/keyDown/animate). Settings model (6 booleans with inverted keys).
6) PlayerCharacter lineup, displayName and tint, plus updateModel dispatch, about 40 lines.
7) HUD layout specification: all coordinates, sizes, colours, strings and the time format in RaceHUD (210), RaceNavigationMap (86), HUDView (100), FrameRateHUD (45) and LevelLoadingView (44), about 485 lines. The layout math ports one-to-one to any 2D API offering rounded rectangles, ellipses, polylines, dashes, clipping, transforms, and text draw and measure. Only the drawing calls change. The terrain raster algorithm (384² height sampling) and the FPS sampling algorithm (0.5 s windows) are pure logic.
8) LevelLoading progress monotonicity and the stage-label sequence, about 10 lines.
9) World.swift scene description, 150 lines. Data and parameters are reusable; SceneKit primitive construction is not (SCNBox chamfer, SCNShape triangulation, SCNText, SCNCylinder).
10) Python build tooling. prepare-simulator-assets.py (69 lines) and the exporters (export-marvin-simulator.py, export-r2d2-simulator.py, export-racers-simulator.py, racer_gltf.py) are stdlib-only and portable. launch-marvin.py (149 lines) is portable except for selectors on pipes, start_new_session and os.killpg. make-marvin-app-icons.py needs a non-macOS ICO path. test-simulator-launch.py (97 lines) is a unittest suite and portable.
Platform-specific code in this subsystem, about 2,160 lines: main.swift 7, App.swift 1,159 (of which about 560 is smoke harness, lines 231-418 and 787-1158), SimulatorView 140, MainMenu 221, RaceHUD 210, RaceNavigationMap 86, FrameRateHUD 45, LevelLoading 86, PlayerCharacter 60, World 150.
inventories.assets:
UI assets are almost entirely procedural; there are no bitmap UI textures, nine-slices or atlases. All panels, maps, bars and markers are vector-drawn every frame.

- Fonts: Apple system fonts only. SF Pro (systemFont, monospacedDigitSystemFont) and SF Mono (monospacedSystemFont) at weights regular, medium, semibold and bold, sizes 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17, 18, 21, 23, 26, 30, 34, 44, 58 and 80 pt. Avenir Next Condensed DemiBold/Medium for town signs. Helvetica-Light in Credits.rtf. Licensing: none of these may be redistributed or used on Windows, so replacements are required (OFL candidates: Inter, JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono, Roboto Mono, Barlow/Roboto Condensed; or Windows system fonts Segoe UI Variable, Cascadia Mono, Consolas).
- Icons: SF Symbols house, video, pause.fill, play.fill, arrow.counterclockwise and keyboard are Apple-only and need replacements (Fluent UI System Icons MIT, Material Symbols Apache-2.0, Lucide ISC, or Segoe Fluent Icons system font).
- App icons in Resources/Icons:
  - AppIconLight/Dark.icns (158-164 KB, iconset 16-512 @1x/@2x).
  - AppIconLight/Dark.png (1024 px).
  - AppIconLight/Dark.svg, generated by scripts/make-marvin-app-icons.py from apps/entire-connector-macos/Resources/entire-symbol-dark-icon.svg using rsvg-convert and iconutil.
  - Windows needs .ico files: 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64 and 256, with 256 stored as PNG. Optionally MSIX Square44x44/150x150 assets with light and dark (altform) variants.
- Bundle contents copied by build-app.sh:
  - Resources/{R2D2 11 MB, BB8 6.6 MB, WallE 42 MB, City 44 MB, Dirt 2.1 MB, Marvin 16 MB (generated from STEP), Audio 49 MB in 163 files}.
  - *.icns.
  - LICENSE-hardware (CERN-OHL-S-2.0).

They are cached through a fingerprint stamp in .build/asset-cache/<exporter>.json; a hash mismatch triggers re-export. scripts/city/check-assets.py validates the city assets.

inventories.quantitative:
- Window: 1280x820 pt initially, minimum 900x640 pt. HUD layout QA is captured at 900x550. The benchmark uses 960x540 pt, which is 1920x1080 drawable pixels at 2x.
- Update and render rates: update Timer 60 Hz; SceneKit preferredFramesPerSecond 60 for both views; dt clamp 0.1 s; intro and outro flights 3.2 s; countdown 3 s.
- MSAA: Sandbox 4x, Dirt 2x, menu portrait 4x.
- Shadow maps: sandbox sun 4096², 16 samples, maximumShadowDistance 22, orthographicScale 10. Menu key light 2048², 32 samples, radius 32. README: Dirt Track sun 2048².
- Dirt SSAO: intensity 0.70, radius 1.6, bias 0.025.
- Model sizes:
  - Marvin: 23 parts and 695,172 triangles (the smoke test asserts 23 parts and more than 600k triangles).
  - R2-D2: 25,158 triangles (asserted).
  - BB-8: 7,198 triangles.
  - WALL-E: 40,158 triangles.
  - Height ratios: Marvin 0.60/1.08 of R2-D2, BB-8 0.67/1.08, WALL-E 1.016/1.08.
- Town (README): 1,327 building modules, 298 people, 130 spatial batches, at most 16 animated nearby people.
- Sandbox scene: 5 obstacles, 5 beacons. Each groove is 2x128 quads (512 triangles). Ring holes use 128 segments and discs have 128 radial segments. Grid lines: 11 along x, 9 along z.
- HUD data volumes:
  - Course polyline 161 points.
  - Town map raster 336x336 pt.
  - Terrain raster 384x384 (147,456 height samples once).
  - Footprint outline 129 points.
  - Scores: 10 stored, 5 shown.
  - Standings: 4 rows.
  - The HUD is redrawn about 60 times a second; the FPS HUD every 0.5 s.
- Loading smoke pass criteria: more than 20 monotonic progress reports, more than 5 responsive main-thread ticks, first value 0 and last 1.
- Measured performance (docs/performance-validation/2026-10-03, MacBook Air M2 24 GB, 1920x1080, SceneKit didRenderScene intervals, not GPU or presentation timing):
  - 120 s timer-driven city roam: mean 59.98 fps, p50 16.67 ms, p95 17.22 ms, p99 17.55 ms, 2 frames over 25 ms, 0 over 50 ms, CPU update p95 2.80 ms.
  - The display-link variant is essentially identical: 59.99 fps, p99 17.46 ms.
  - 603 s ten-minute drive (timer): mean 57.23 fps, p50 16.67 ms, p95 18.58 ms, p99 34.22 ms, 1,662 frames over 25 ms, 1 over 50 ms, worst 52.3 ms, CPU update p95 2.63 ms. Displayed FPS: min 40.7, median 60.0, max 60.3, from 1,176 HUD samples. Travel 1,339.7 m. thermalState 1 (fair).
  - Metal HUD diagnostic: maximum GPU time 16.43 ms.
  - Proposed GPU gate: p99 at most 12.5 ms and maximum below 16.667 ms.
  - The frame budget is 16.667 ms at 60 Hz. The user objected to dips to 58 fps.
- Benchmark default duration 45 s (MARVIN_BENCHMARK_SECONDS, minimum 10). The first 3 s are excluded from timing; HUD samples count from 3.5 s.
- Build output: 174 MB .app; Resources about 171 MB; 163 audio files.
- Command-line surface: 63 app flags (listed in open_questions context below) plus about 23 MARVIN_* environment variables.
inventories.validation_existing:
The native smoke harness lives in the same binary. Each mode takes an output directory after the flag, runs on a fixed 1/60 clock with the storm disabled (weatherOverride=false), dispatches after 20 menu frames, writes PNG and JSON, and exits 0 or 1. Relevant to this subsystem:
- `--menu-smoke-test DIR`: renders the main menu, composites the AppKit controls with the Metal portrait snapshot into main-menu.png, and drags the portrait through synthetic NSEvents (yaw +0.8 and back). It presses the hidden letters b/r/w/m (writing menu-<key>.png and checking the 0.4 rad drag per model), navigates Down/Down/Return into Settings, runs checkDrivingAssistSettings (UserDefaults round trip, a fresh view reads the persisted values, all 6 buttons fit at 900x550, driving-assist-settings.png), presses Back, then Sandbox.
- `--smoke-test DIR` (smoke.json): drive, boost and steer input via synthetic keys and flagsChanged; pause freezes elapsed time; brake; clearInput (focusPassed); head keys; reset; camera level-ness in all 3 modes across 5 azimuths; light and dark icon switching through NSApp.appearance; dirt start, intro start and mid-point; the race HUD captured at 900x550 (dirt-hud.png); score recording, deduplicated across two calls and round-tripped to test-scores.json; mode return to Sandbox; plus many rendering and physics checks owned by other readers.
- `--character-smoke-test DIR` (characters.json): each robot selected from the menu, played in Sandbox and Dirt, checking HUD names and lineup.
- `--loading-smoke-test DIR`: captures loading.png at 49-51% progress and asserts monotonic history with more than 20 reports, more than 5 heartbeats and a final reveal.
- `--viewport-smoke-test DIR` (viewport.json): hiding the toolbar and HUD changes neither the viewport nor the projection at 3 window sizes; overlays sit below the toolbar; restart is stable; normal resizes still reach the renderer.
- `--display-link-lifecycle-check DIR` (lifecycle.json, fps-overlay.png): real-time display-link clock, FPS readout live and click-through, pause freezes the clock and audio, miniaturise freezes the clock and audio, restore without catch-up, audio resumes.
- `--town-benchmark DIR` (benchmark.json, timeline.json, resources.json, displayed-fps.json, final-fps.png): FPS HUD sampling and frame-cadence statistics.
Core checks: `swift run --package-path apps/simulator-macos SimulationChecks` (custom runner, 15 files, 1,671 lines) covers simulation, race, scoring including the DirtScores save/load filter and ranking round trip, standings, assists, collisions and frame-rate independence at 10, 30, 60 and 120 fps.
Tooling: `python3 scripts/test-simulator-launch.py` tests asset-cache invalidation and the launcher status protocol.
Evidence archives: docs/performance-validation/2026-10-03 (ten-minute drive, display-link versus timer comparisons, fps-ui.json lifecycle pass, Metal HUD GPU samples).
Not covered by automated checks: AppKit menu-bar shortcuts, toolbar clicks, mouse orbit and zoom sensitivity, the About panel, the alert paths, real (non-synthetic) occlusion by other windows, and settings persistence across a real relaunch.
risks: Font licensing: SF Pro, SF Mono and Avenir Next cannot ship on Windows. Every HUD and menu string changes glyph shape and width, and RaceHUD and the help panels size themselves from measured text, so the layouts shift. Pixel-identical UI is impossible; acceptable 'same graphics' tolerances must be agreed.
SF Symbols in the toolbar are Apple-licensed and need substitute icons.

On macOS the 3D scene shows blurred through the translucent unified title bar and toolbar (fullSizeContentView), and overlays use the safe-area layout guide. Reproducing this on Windows needs DWM backdrop and custom non-client handling (Win11 22H2+ for Mica/Acrylic), or a decision to drop it.

Pause-on-occlusion: macOS freezes the race when the window is fully covered (occlusionState). Windows cannot detect this reliably in windowed mode, so pause behaviour and the race-clock exclusion rules will differ unless restated.
Windows modal loops (live resize or move, Win32 menu tracking, Alt or F10 menu mode) block a naive game loop. The macOS Timer in .common modes keeps simulating during these interactions.

Keyboard pitfalls specific to Windows: Shift is boost, and repeated taps trigger the Sticky Keys prompt. Alt or F10 enter menu mode and steal WASD. The Windows key opens Start. IME can swallow keys. Space activates focused native buttons. Cmd shortcuts must be remapped to Ctrl, and the on-screen '⌘R' strings in SimulatorView.swift:100, RaceHUD.swift:88/93/116/128/153 must be rewritten.

Positional versus character keys: gameplay uses physical mac key codes (WASD stays positional on AZERTY), while the menu letters m/b/r/w use characters. Windows must use scancodes for gameplay and WM_CHAR or text input for the letters to keep the same behaviour.

Mouse and trackpad sensitivity constants (0.008 rad/pt orbit, 0.035 per scroll unit) are tuned to macOS acceleration and precise scrolling deltas. WHEEL_DELTA 120 notches and precision touchpads need calibration and a natural-scrolling decision.

60 fps cap and pacing: preferredFramesPerSecond=60 caps rendering even on 120 Hz screens; Windows high-refresh monitors need an explicit limiter plus flip-model vsync. The macOS model of a main-thread 60 Hz Timer plus a separate render thread differs from a single game loop, so measured cadence statistics are not directly comparable.

Background world construction: DirtWorld and its SceneKit node trees are built on a GCD background queue. Most engines require main-thread scene creation, so loading must split into data generation and instantiation, which affects progress granularity and the loading smoke criteria (more than 20 reports, more than 5 responsive ticks).
Synchronous model loading in applicationDidFinishLaunching blocks before the first frame. On Windows a pump blocked for over 5 s shows the 'Not Responding' ghost window.

HUD compositing: Core Animation composites the overlays in sRGB over the Metal layer. An engine compositing UI in linear or HDR space changes the look of the translucent panels (alpha 0.9, 0.94, 0.42 dims). Text antialiasing (ClearType versus grayscale) also differs.

Fractional DPI scaling (125/150/175%) versus macOS integer 2x changes 1-pt rules, 7-8 px markers and text crispness. Minimum window size and benchmark sizes must be specified in DIPs or pixels deliberately.
The dynamic light/dark app icon is only partially achievable on Windows: pinned taskbar and Explorer icons are static unless MSIX packaging with theme-aware assets is used.

Score-file compatibility: Foundation's default Date encoding (seconds since 2001-01-01) must be replicated if mac score files are imported or shared. Atomic replace on Windows (ReplaceFileW) can fail transiently because of AV or indexer locks.
Hybrid-GPU laptops: macOS opts into automatic graphics switching. Windows may run on the iGPU unless the dGPU is requested, which risks the 60 fps target.
Distribution: ad-hoc codesign has no Windows analogue. Unsigned exes or MSIs hit SmartScreen; an Authenticode certificate or Azure Trusted Signing is needed for a frictionless install.

Test harness portability: about 560 lines of App.swift plus 20+ smoke files depend on NSEvent synthesis, SCNView.snapshot and NSView.cacheDisplay. Without an input-event abstraction and a readback path, the Windows port loses its regression net, including the viewport-drift and lifecycle checks that encode user requirements.
launch-marvin.py uses selectors on subprocess pipes and os.killpg/start_new_session, which do not work on Windows. make-marvin-app-icons.py needs rsvg-convert and iconutil.
If an engine with float-only transforms is chosen, the double-precision camera and physics math (SIMD3<Double>) may diverge from the macOS results the tests assert.
open_questions: Should Windows reproduce the macOS chrome (unified translucent toolbar plus a menu bar with About/Quit/Simulation items), or adopt a Windows idiom such as an in-game toolbar overlay or system menu with Ctrl shortcuts? 'Same features' requires the commands; 'same graphics' is ambiguous for OS chrome.
Which font substitutes are acceptable for SF Pro, SF Mono and Avenir Next Condensed? Should text metrics be matched (e.g. Inter with tuned tracking) to keep HUD panel sizes identical?
Should the Windows build pause when the window is fully covered by other windows (the macOS occlusion behaviour), or only when minimised or inactive?

Where should settings and scores live: registry or JSON for settings, and RoamingAppData versus LocalAppData for motocross-v4-scores.json? Should macOS score files be importable, which requires the 2001-epoch Date encoding?
Gamepad (XInput or GameInput) support is absent on macOS. Is it expected on Windows, or is it out of scope under 'same features'?
Is an explicit fullscreen or borderless mode required? macOS offers only implicit green-button full screen with no menu item.
Should rendering stay capped at 60 fps on high-refresh Windows monitors to match preferredFramesPerSecond=60, or be uncapped?
Which Windows performance target replaces the M2 MacBook Air at 1920x1080, 60 fps (GPU tier, iGPU versus dGPU, minimum Windows version)?
For the dynamic light/dark icon, follow AppsUseLightTheme or SystemUsesLightTheme (taskbar colour)? Is MSIX packaging acceptable for theme-aware taskbar assets?
Distribution format and signing: portable zip, MSI or MSIX? Is an Authenticode certificate or Azure Trusted Signing available?

inventories.subsystem: Rendering pipeline and shading (SceneKit-on-Metal renderer, lights/shadows/sky/post-FX, all custom shader modifiers, custom geometry, direct Metal usage, GPU diagnostics)
files_read: /Users/m1/marvin/apps/simulator-macos/Sources/MarvinSimulator/TownWorld.swift (lines 1-400, 1680-2062: shadow casters, streets shader, LOD cells, TownMesh, TownPainter.adobe)
inventories.overview:
All rendering is SceneKit on Metal (benchmark asserts view.renderingAPI == .metal). The shipped game uses no SCNProgram, SCNTechnique, CIFilter or SCNParticleSystem. Every custom effect is a SceneKit shader modifier: a Metal Shading Language snippet injected at the .geometry, .surface or .fragment entry point. There are about 20 distinct modifiers, roughly 330 lines of MSL. Note: SimulatorView.swift holds only the input-handling SCNView subclass and the sandbox AppKit HUD. Renderer setup lives in App.swift (applicationDidFinishLaunching, startSandbox, startDirtTrack), World.swift (sandbox), MainMenu.swift (portrait view) and DirtWorld.swift plus BinarySky.swift (race and town).

There are three scenes in two SCNViews:
(1) Main-menu portrait: 4x MSAA, LDR. One ambient light and one deferred-shadow directional light. An SCNFloor with an unlit material acts as a shadow catcher.
(2) Sandbox: 4x MSAA, LDR, linear fog from 15 to 38 m. One deferred-shadow sun with a 4096 map fitted to the camera. Flat background colour.
(3) Race, town and dunes:
- 2x MSAA and HDR with fixed exposure.
- Bloom 0.38 / 1.2 / 12 and SceneKit SSAO 0.70 / 1.6 / 0.025.
- Linear fog tinted with the horizon colour: 115 to 240 m clear, 3 to 65 m in a storm.
- A procedural twin-sun sky dome drawn by a fragment modifier.
- Two directional suns, each with its own forward-mode orthographic shadow map (4096 and 2048, 116 m wide). The maps are world-anchored and texel-snapped, not camera-fitted.
- One ambient light, plus image-based lighting from a 64x32 procedural gradient that is regenerated per race.

Materials are mostly .physicallyBased with 2048 scanned maps. sRGB vertex-colour palettes are linearised in shaders with pow 2.2. Ground uses world-space procedural value-noise pigments. Many premultiplied, depth-write-off ground overlays sit millimetres apart.

All geometry is custom SCNGeometry:
- Built once at load: batched town cells with 2 LODs, crowd batches carrying 8 UV channels that drive GPU vertex animation, and dune tiles with 3 LODs.
- Rebuilt every frame: dust and clod particle batches, tread decals and storm grains.

A welded shadow-only proxy mesh is routed into the sun shadow maps through categoryBitMask. Direct Metal is limited to:
- tiny data textures (robot dirt-coating uniforms, dune height deltas)
- one shared MTLBuffer vertex source
- offscreen SCNRenderer diagnostics (LoadedGPUProbe, AOPreparationProbe)
- GPU capture.

RendererStudy is an opt-in RealityKit comparison and does not ship.

The performance target is an M2 MacBook Air at 1920x1080 and 60 Hz. Measured GPU time is about 11.3 to 16 ms per frame with about 2,180 draws, so headroom is tight.

platform_dependencies.fidelity_risk: Semantic differences can shift results. _surface.position and normal are view space; ground shaders reconstruct world XZ via inverseViewTransform. SCNFloor reflectivity 0 with a .constant material 0xf2f1e9 that must still receive the deferred shadow (shadow catcher blending seamlessly into the AppKit background).

SCNCamera FOV 48 deg (SceneKit default vertical projection direction), zNear 0.02, zFar 250 in race (80 in sandbox). Chase mode 0: distance 4.5 (race), elevation 0.30 rad, target groundY+0.35 with 1.5 m look-ahead, eye smoothing mix = 1-exp(-7.67 dt). Boom shortening against scenery and dunes, with lengthening smoothing 1-exp(-3.5 dt) and a 0.16-0.18 m clearance. Orbit mode 1: yaw += 0.008 rad/px, pitch clamped 0.15 to 1.35, zoom 1.6 to 9 at 0.035 per scroll unit. Overview mode 2: eye (0,38,-33) looking at origin, or following the player offset (0,+38,-33) in town, via OverviewMotion smoothing. Intro 3.2 s: starts after 0.35 s from (0,38,-33) with quintic smootherstep t^3(t(6t-15)+10). Outro to the overview over the same 3.2 s, and the camera stays locked after the finish. No camera shake, FOV change, depth of field or motion blur.

Race only: wantsHDR true, wantsExposureAdaptation false, exposureOffset 0 (fixed exposure, so a tiny sun entering frame does not pump). All other SCNCamera HDR/colour parameters at SceneKit defaults: averageGray, whitePoint, min/maxExposure, contrast, saturation, colorGrading none. motionBlurIntensity, vignettingIntensity and colorFringeIntensity are 0 (defaults; the AO probe explicitly zeroes them). Sandbox and menu are LDR.

bloomIntensity 0.38, bloomThreshold 1.2, bloomBlurRadius 12; iteration count and spread at defaults. Main sources: the sun discs, at linear luminance tint*(3.8+2.4*limb) for sun A and tint*(2.5+1.5*limb) for sun B, plus haze peaks. Geometry must occlude the sun and its bloom (no flare overlay). Test: a black screen in front of the sun drops centre-patch luminance from >0.6 to <0.05.

Race: screenSpaceAmbientOcclusionIntensity 0.70, Radius 1.6 (m), Bias 0.025. Normal and depth thresholds are SceneKit defaults. Sandbox: 0. SceneKit implementation as observed in Xcode replay: a full-resolution RGBA16Float normal/depth prepass with its own depth attachment (about 20% of the frame, re-drawing scene geometry including alpha overlays), then scn_ssao_compute as one full-screen triangle writing a half-resolution 960x540 RGBA16Float result (about 10%). The result feeds the PBR ambient term (_surface.ambientOcclusion under USE_SSAO), so it darkens ambient and IBL lighting, not direct sunlight. Required visual role: contact shading for robots, residents, dust, trails and walls in both suns and in storms.

Linear (SceneKit fogDensityExponent default 1). Clear: fogColor = horizon colour (calibrated RGB, recomputed per sky), start 115 m, end 240 m. Storm: colour 0xae865b (sRGB), 3 to 65 m. Sandbox: 0xdbe4df, 15 to 38 m. The sky dome is written to bypass fog ('infinitely distant sky' comment): it sets _output.color directly in a fragment modifier.

SCNSphere radius 220, segmentCount 48. Material .constant, cullMode .front (inside faces), readsFromDepthBuffer false, writesToDepthBuffer false. Node renderingOrder -10000 (drawn first), castsShadow false. Each frame its position is constrained to the camera's presentation world position (SCNTransformConstraint). Must sit inside zFar 250. Hidden in the AO normal prepass.

Geometry modifier: varying skyDirection = object-space position. Fragment, with d = normalize(skyDirection) and height = max(d.y,0):
- h = 1-exp(-height/mix(0.085,0.35,daylight)); sky = mix(horizon,zenith,h).
- axis = normalize(sunA+sunB); facing = pow(max(0, dot(d.xz,axis.xz)/(max(len(d.xz),1e-5)*max(len(axis.xz),1e-5))), 3).
- band = exp(-((height-0.12)/0.10)^2); sky += duskBand*band*(1-daylight)*(0.35+0.65*facing).
- sky += (0.34,0.095,0.018)*facing*exp(-height/0.15)*(1-daylight).
- a = acos(clamp(dot(d,sunA))), b likewise for sunB; haze = mix(1,0.35,daylight).
- sky += tintA*haze*(0.5*exp(-a^2/0.006)+0.65*exp(-a/0.017)).
- sky += tintB*haze*(0.3*exp(-b^2/0.004)+0.4*exp(-b/0.013)).
- discA = 1-smoothstep(rA*0.91, rA*1.05, a), discB likewise; limbA = sqrt(max(0,1-(a/rA)^2)), limbB likewise.
- sky = mix(sky, tintA*(3.8+2.4*limbA), discA); sky = mix(sky, tintB*(2.5+1.5*limbB), discB).
- output = float4(mix(sky, stormTint+sky*0.025, storm*0.97), 1).
Uniforms: sunA, sunB, zenith, horizon, tintA, tintB, sunRadii = (0.55 deg, 0.38 deg) in radians, daylight, duskBand, storm (0/1), stormTint (0.46,0.29,0.14). Below the horizon, height clamps to 0, giving horizon colour plus haze.

day = min(1, maxSunElevationY/0.55). evening = 1 if fraction > 0.5.
- lowZenith = (0.018,0.070,0.17), or (0.065,0.027,0.10) in the evening.
- lowHorizon = (0.95,0.36,0.09), or (0.85,0.19,0.035) in the evening.
- zenith = lowZenith + ((0.20,0.38,0.62) - lowZenith)*day.
- horizon = lowHorizon + ((0.65,0.72,0.75) - lowHorizon)*day.
- duskBand = (0.04,0.055,0.06), or (0.22,0.045,0.085) in the evening.
Values are passed straight to the shader as linear floats.

Fictional circumbinary planet: latitude 25 deg, equinox.
- Hour-angle offsets: atan2(-0.06 sin(phase), 1+0.06 cos(phase)) and atan2(0.14 sin(phase), 1-0.14 cos(phase)).
- Daylight window = interval where both suns are above the horizon; fraction is clamped to 0.015-0.985 of that window.
- direction = (-sin(h+d), cos(lat)cos(h+d), -sin(lat)cos(h+d)).
- Random race: phase uniform in [0.35, pi-0.35] (+pi with 50% chance), fraction uniform in [0.015, 0.985].
- Separation is always 1.1-13 deg; frozen during a race and redrawn on reset.
- Benchmark override: MARVIN_DAYLIGHT_FRACTION with phase 1.2.

Two .directional SCNLights.
- Sun 1 intensity 1550, Sun 2 intensity 470, each x0.20 during a storm.
- Colour = intrinsic x Beer-Lambert extinction. Intrinsic: (1,0.94,0.83) for sun 1, (1,0.73,0.46) for sun 2. Extinction exp(-k*m) with k = (0.035,0.070,0.15) and Kasten-Young air mass m = 1/(sinAlt + 0.50572*(altDeg+6.07995)^-1.6364).
- Colour is set via NSColor(calibratedRed:). The same tint feeds the sky disc and haze.
- Each light is placed at direction*80 and looks at the origin.

Both suns: castsShadow true, shadowMode .forward (shadows attenuate each light separately, so one sun lights the other's shadow).
- shadowMapSize 4096x4096 (sun 1) and 2048x2048 (sun 2).
- automaticallyAdjustsShadowProjection false; sampleDistributedShadowMaps false (one map, no cascades); forcesBackFaceCasters false.
- zNear 0.1, zFar 220, maximumShadowDistance 500, orthographicScale 58 (116 m square footprint; texel 2.83 cm / 5.66 cm).
- shadowRadius 3 / 2, shadowSampleCount 8, shadowColor opaque black, shadowBias 0.6.
- The sustained gate requires shadowMapWidths [2048,4096].

Called every frame. center = origin while max(|x|,|z|) < 28, otherwise the player position; origin after the race finishes. The anchor is center projected onto the light's right/up/back axes, each component snapped to texel = 116/mapWidth. Light position = anchor + back*80. Shadows never refit to camera rotation.
Clear sky: .ambient, colour calibrated (0.54,0.62,0.78), intensity 260-70*day. Storm: colour 0xd4b48a, intensity 320.

scene.lightingEnvironment.contents = 64x32 RGBA8 equirectangular NSImage (deviceRGB), rebuilt on every sky apply. Row y: t = pow(max(0, cos(y/31*pi)), 0.42); rgb = horizon*(1-t) + zenith*t, multiplied by 0.55 for y > 16. Clamped to 0-255, so LDR. Intensity 0.95-0.20*day. Storm: probe built from zenith (0.46,0.34,0.23) and horizon (0.68,0.50,0.32), intensity 0.75. There is deliberately no baked sun in the probe; the directional lights supply sun specular. City/sky.hdr (Poly Haven Kloppenheim 02, 1024x512) is not used by the shipped renderer, only by the RealityKit study.

Casters:
- Robots: all parts, including track shoes and wheels.
- Walking residents and street pedestrians, with GPU-animated shadows.
- Town cells: only those within +-48 m during racing, or within 75 m of the focus when it is outside +-28 (focus = camera XZ shifted by +33 z if camera y >= 12).
- Displaced dune patches.
- Track lanes, berms and walls, base terrain, city gate and posts (SceneKit defaults).
Non-casters: crowd cells, dune tiles, horizon plane, all ground overlays and decals, dust, clods, storm, signs, start boxes, checkers, arrows, sky, eyes, embankments, exploration-detail cells.
Optional --benchmark-shadow-culling also tests sun-swept AABBs (bounds +1 m, projected to y=-2 along both suns) against the camera frustum with a +1 deg guard.
fidelity_spec.where: TownWorld.swift:54-100,196,205; ShadowVolume.swift:4-42; TownCrowd.swift:283,298; TownResidents.swift:102; TownStreetResidents.swift:55; DesertWorld.swift:64; DeformableSand.swift:21; DirtWorld.swift:137,154,165,178,350,370

fidelity_spec.parameters: For each 'Town cell' node: a sibling proxy built from the cell geometry and each LOD. Positions are welded only on exact Float equality. Two element groups (single-sided, double-sided) use .constant materials. Proxy categoryBitMask = 1<<20; the camera mask drops that bit and both shadow lights add it. Originals get castsShadow=false while the proxy follows each frame's caster decision. Requires materials to be from {plaster, adobe, cloth, metal} and triangle-only; otherwise it falls back. --benchmark-shadow-batch-reference disables it.

PBR via material(0x986441, roughness 0.94), isDoubleSided true.
- diffuse Dirt/diffuse.jpg, normal Dirt/normal.jpg (intensity 0.65), roughness Dirt/roughness.jpg; all 1024 squared, repeat, contentsTransform scale (48,1,1).
- UV u = fraction of the lap over 768 samples; v = across a 3.9 m texture width shared by lane, berms and shoulders.
- multiply = procedural soilTexture(track) 1024x256 at intensity 0.35, untransformed UVs: grain/blotch noise, 190-cycle groove sine, centred lane darkening exp(-((v-0.52)/0.27)^2).
- Surface modifier: luma = dot(diffuse,(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722)); diffuse = (0.34,0.205,0.145) + luma*(0.58,0.44,0.33).
- Lane rut displacement 0.0015*sin(across*180 + 0.8 sin(9 phase))*sin(pi across). Berms raised 0.10 m outer and 0.055 m inner with a sin(pi across) profile.

fidelity_spec.feature: Earth, terrain and dune base material
fidelity_spec.parameters: earth: PBR material(0x827656, roughness 1), double-sided. diffuse = packedEarthTexture 512 squared (tone ~(157,140,115) +- noise, pebbles), repeat, contentsTransform scale 64 on a 256 m plane (4 m repeat). No normal map. Surface modifier = TownGround.terrainSurface plus the infield deposit block. Base plane 256x256 at y -0.025, rotated -pi/2, partitioned into shaded and depth-only regions. Horizon plane 4000x4000 at y -0.05 uses earth. Dune tiles use 'sand' = earth copy with identity transform (UV = world/4), roughness 0.94, terrainSurface only (copied before the deposit was appended).

p = world XZ = (scn_frame.inverseViewTransform * float4(_surface.position,1)).xz.
- radius = 123 + 13 sin(3a+0.4) + 9 cos(5a-0.7) + 6 sin(2a), where a = atan2(p.y,p.x).
- desert = smoothstep(radius-12, radius+32, |p|).
- grain = dot(diffuse,(0.299,0.587,0.114)); bands = townNoise(p/43).
- dune = (0.64,0.43,0.23)*(0.83+0.30 grain) + bands*(0.075,0.058,0.029).
- soil = mix(diffuse, townPigment(p)*(1.30+grain), smoothstep(28,42,|p|)).
- diffuse = mix(soil, dune, desert).
- ripple = sin(17x + 5.8z + 1.8 sin(0.41z) + sin(0.22x)); normal = normalize(normal + (0.022 ripple, 0, 0.008 ripple)*desert).
townNoise: 2D value noise with smoothstep fade, hash fract(sin(dot(cell,(127.1,311.7)))*43758.5453).
townPigment(p):
- warp = (noise(p/31), noise(p/37+19))*9.
- broad = noise((p+warp)/22); fine = noise((p+warp)/5.5).
- pale = smoothstep(0.28, 0.72, 0.5 broad + 0.5 fine).
- soil = mix((0.255,0.208,0.145), (0.46,0.36,0.235), pale) * (0.89 + 0.22 noise(p/2.1+7)).

768 squared premultiplied RGBA texture covering a 60x60 m square centred on the origin. Infield coverage is from the course edge and service-yard traffic masks; outside the track, wind-thrown fans with falloff^1.65; alpha <= 0.94. Base colour (184,144,118) +- grain. Sampled at uv = (worldXZ+30)/60 with a clamp_to_zero linear sampler, mip linear. diffuse = diffuse*(1-a) + rgb, appended to earth's surface modifier.

Base terrain is a 4 m grid over +-128 m. Quads whose nearest distance is >= 38 m and farthest <= 93 m go to a second element with a depth-only material: .constant, colorBufferWriteMask [], same depth-write, depth-read, cull and double-sided flags. The opaque trampled overlay hides them. This is a pure optimisation and must be visually identical.

4 m quads over +-176 m at y -0.023, skipping all-zero alpha quads.
- PBR: ground-base, ground-normal (intensity 0.65) and ground-rough JPGs, 2048 squared, UV world/4, repeat, mip linear, anisotropy 8.
- writesToDepthBuffer false, transparencyMode .aOne, castsShadow false.
- Surface: diffuse = townPigment(worldXZ)*(0.52 + 2.5*luma).
- Fragment (#pragma transparent): radius = 130 + 13 sin(3a+0.4) + 9 cos(5a-0.7) + 6 sin(2a); blend = smoothstep(28,36,|p|)*(1 - smoothstep(-7,5,|p|-radius)); output premultiplied rgb*blend, a = blend. The vertex groundBlend varying is computed but unused.
- Profiling: this draw (21,786 indices) costs 5-8% of a warm frame.

Irregular 18-segment ellipse fans at y -0.019. Opacity is full in the centre, 0.72 at the 0.38 ring, 0 at the rim. Inks: 0x8e806a alpha 0.22 (doors, 2 of 3 compounds); 0xc2ac87 alpha 0.17 (mid-route); yards 0x786753 alpha 0.38 or 0xbba07b alpha 0.25 (1.4x1.0 m). Material: PBR white, roughness 1, .aOne, no depth write. Geometry: groundTint = half4(pow(max(color.rgb,0),2.2), color.a). Surface: diffuse = tint. Fragment (#pragma transparent): rgb *= a; a = vertex a.

13 Hermite-smoothed streets sampled every ~0.9 m. Four edge offsets: -w/2-0.6, -0.3w, +0.3w, w/2+0.6, with an irregular width factor 1 + 0.07 sin(0.63x+0.31z) + 0.04 sin(1.43z). Height y = -0.016 (+0.001 for secondary). Inks 0x9d8d75 alpha 0.44 (primary) and 0xa99a81 alpha 0.23 (secondary); zero alpha at outer edges; 14 m smoothstep fade at open ends.
Material: PBR white, roughness 1, .aOne, no depth write. Geometry: streetTint (pow 2.2). Surface: diffuse = tint.
Fragment, with edge = |p| - radius(130 + ...):
- exposure = smoothstep(-18, 22, edge).
- wind = (0.86x + 0.51z, -0.51x + 0.86z); tongues = townNoise(wind/(2.8,0.75)).
- broken = smoothstep(0.28, 0.72, 0.65 tongues + 0.70 exposure).
- remaining = (1 - smoothstep(-4,22,edge))*(1 - exposure*broken).
- alpha = vertexAlpha*remaining, premultiplied.

fidelity_spec.feature: Clay pigment overlays on sand (service yard, city-exit ramp)
fidelity_spec.parameters: Same mesh as the sand base: service yard 62 rows, exit ramp 100x96 at 8 cm. Clay-UV re-mapped and raised 0.0002 m. Vertex colour r = red-soil weight (smoothstep foot fade, noise 0.85/0.7 blends). Material: clay copy. Geometry: half redSoil = color.r. Fragment (#pragma transparent): rgb *= redSoil; a = redSoil. .aOne, no depth write, castsShadow false. The sand base under it is an earth copy with identity transform.

fidelity_spec.feature: City scanned materials and palette tint
fidelity_spec.parameters:
PBR. Scans are 2048 squared JPG base, OpenGL normal and rough; repeat, mipFilter linear, maxAnisotropy 4. normal.intensity: plaster 1.0, adobe 0.85, cloth 0.28, metal 0.55. Metalness: metal 0.55, others 0.
Geometry modifier: half3 cityTint = pow(max(color.rgb,0), 2.2).
Surface diffuse (luma = dot(diffuse,(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722))):
- plaster: tint*(0.50 + 1.1 luma)
- adobe: tint*(0.60 + 1.25 luma)
- cloth: tint*(0.82 + 0.22 luma)
- metal: tint*(0.62 + 0.65 luma)
- skin (white, roughness 0.64) and leather (roughness 0.78): diffuse = tint
cloth and crowdCloth are double-sided.
plaster and adobe: multiply = plasterWear atlas, 1024 squared (8x8 tiles of 128), mappingChannel 1, clamp, mip linear (anisotropy 4 on plaster). Wear-tile histories: 0 neutral; 1 base grime 0.19; 2 a repaired patch; 3 a roof runoff streak. Levels are clamped >= 0.60 with a warm bias (G -0.09, B -0.19 of the darkening).

Flat-shaded triangles, or smooth for adobe bevels.
- Vertex colour = ink*shade, with shade = (0.94 + 0.06*max(0,n.y))*(0.83 + 0.17*min(1, max(0,y)/1.2)). This is baked contact darkening near the ground.
- UV0: world-projected on the dominant normal axis, x0.48.
- UV1: wear-atlas cell (tile = history*16 + seed%16; history buckets 30/40/22/8% per building), inset 0.05-0.95. Default (0.0625,0.0625) = neutral tile 0.
- Material slots [plaster, cloth, metal, adobe]; adobe on 80% of compounds beyond 30 m.
- Vertices merged only when every attribute matches, including tangent and bitangent quantised to 1/65536 after normal projection (maximum merged-basis error 0.001 deg).
- Track brick walls: 0.43 m bricks, 0.13 m courses, palette {0xa28a70, 0x998068, 0xb0997c, 0x927963, 0xa78c70, 0xb29b80}, plaster material.

fidelity_spec.feature: Town LOD and exploration detail fade
fidelity_spec.parameters: Cells are 16 m (inside +-48) or 32 m; near switches to far at SCNLevelOfDetail worldSpaceDistance 82. 'Exploration detail' cells (16 m) show only when the focus is outside +-28 and the camera is below 60 m. Opacity = smoothstep(clamp((58-d)/16)) via SCNNode.opacity: fully visible within 42 m and gone at 58 m. While fading they render as blended transparents.

12 authored models (male/female, stand/sit, 3 variants) with 3 LODs of about 6,500 / 1,600 / 350 triangles. Static spectators are batched per 8 m cell (77 cells), LOD at 10/26 m. Animated individuals use LOD at 8/24 m.
Vertex streams: position, normal, uv x12, colour (sRGB palette bytes; skins {0xb68b70, 0x835c48, 0xc2a084, 0x9c755c, 0xa37c61, 0xc4a591}, outfits {0x746354, 0x566866, 0xa99b81, 0x6d6a53, 0x5b6266, 0x907451, 0x82756b, 0xb8ab91}, plus fixed accents), and texcoord channels 1-7 = originXZ, (yaw, baseY), (phase, neck height), (arm weight, side), (hip, knee), (activity kind, semantic), (shoulder bind x, arm top).
Three element groups: skin, cloth, leather. 1 in 5 people get a 32-triangle shoulder mantle. Bounding box padded (+-0.35, -0.12/+0.2). Cells castsShadow false; walkers true.

Geometry modifier, prepended to the palette conversion. Uniforms crowdTime, walkCycle, walkBlend (per material copy for walkers; shared for static cells).
- Un-rotate by the stored yaw. tempo = 0.8 + 0.4 fract(0.73 phase).
- Idle torso turn: 0.12 sin(0.53 tempo t + phase), weighted smoothstep(hip, hip+0.24).
- Head yaw: 0.44 sin(0.47 tempo t + phase) + 0.12 sin(0.19 t + 2 phase), weighted smoothstep(neck-0.012, neck+0.045); x0.28 for purposeful residents.
- Wave window: pow(max(0, sin(0.31 t + phase)), 6) times a gesture factor by kind; elbow 0.9 + 0.23 sin(5t + phase) about elbow = shoulder + (0.025 side, -0.18, 0.04); shoulder 0.92.
- Walk: arm swing 0.18 sin(cycle); legs 0.24 cos(legPhase) about the hip at x +-0.06; knee bend 0.42 max(0, sin) with a knee weight; hip bob joints.x*(1 - cos(0.24 cos(cycle))).
- Normals are rotated identically. The CPU mirror FootPlacement plants the lowest sole.

Geometry-owned surface modifier on every non-constant robot mesh; geometry is copied, and a zero UV stream is added when missing.
Arguments: dirtToBody float4x4, dirtHeight, dirtWheelX = wheelOffset/height, dirtRolling (1 for BB-8 'ball:' parts and WALL-E 'link:' parts), duneContact = 2x1 RGBA32Float texture: texel0 = dune plane (gx, gz, intercept, active), texel1.r = dirt level quantised to 1/32.
Body, with p = body-space position / height:
- low = mix(1 - smoothstep(0.08, 0.58, p.y), 1, rolling).
- nearWheel = exp(-((|p.x| - wheelX)*9)^2); rear = 1 - smoothstep(-0.22, 0.24, p.z).
- patches = noise3(28p); specks = smoothstep(0.58, 0.76, noise3(145p)).
- splash = smoothstep(0.38, 0.68, patches)*low*(0.45 + 0.35 nearWheel + 0.20 rear).
- dust = (0.04 + 0.22 low)*(0.55 + 0.45 patches).
- coverage = clamp(amount*(dust + 0.85 splash + 0.40 specks*low), 0, 0.92).
- soil = mix((0.19,0.105,0.045), (0.42,0.29,0.16), patches). diffuse lerps to soil; roughness lerps to 1; metalness and selfIllumination are multiplied by (1-coverage).
- Dune rim (when active): world height vs plane; rim = 1 - smoothstep(-0.004, 0.035, dy + (grain-0.5)*0.016); sand = (0.64,0.43,0.23)*(0.84 + 0.25 grain); diffuse lerps by 0.88 rim, roughness lerps to 0.96.
noise3 is a trilinear value noise with hash fract(sin(dot(p,(127.1,311.7,74.7)))*43758.5453). amount += travel/75 m on dirt. The plane updates at 30 Hz in dunes.

Opaque replacement patches per touched 4 m tile: 65x65 vertices (6.25 cm), 8,192 triangles. Vertices come from a shared MTLBuffer (float3 position + float3 normal, stride 32). The base tile (2 m grid, 33x33) loses the triangles underneath.
Geometry modifier: reads the 67x67 R32Float delta texture by integer coordinates (nearest, no mip); y += h; normal = normalize(n + (-dx, 0, -dz)*n.y) with central differences x8.
Bounding box padded -0.14/+0.11. Updated at 30 Hz; texture upload skipped if every change is < 0.5 mm. Uses the sand material; castsShadow true.

560 tiles of 64 m (24x24 minus the centre 4x4) with a 2 m grid. LODs at 2/4/8 m triangle size switch at 0/130/260 m; every LOD keeps the exact 2 m border vertices, fan-stitched, so there are no cracks or skirts. Normals come from the analytic DesertTerrain gradient; UV = world/4. castsShadow false. Plus a 4000 m horizon plane at y -0.05.

10 cm cells over +-23.2 m, built only where deposit > 1e-5. Vertex colour = (depth, d/dx, d/dz). PBR, diffuse = packedEarthTexture with UV world/2 (repeat), roughness 1.
- Geometry: driftDepth = color.r*deposition (uniform = storm.accumulation, initial 0.18); y += driftDepth; normal tilted by -(g, b)*deposition.
- Surface (#pragma transparent): diffuse = (0.57,0.38,0.23)*(0.82 + 0.5 grain).
- Fragment: discard if depth < 0.0004; coverage = smoothstep(0.0004, 0.025, depth), premultiplied.
castsShadow false; hidden when there is no storm.

960 world-space particles advected by wind and wrapped to +-32 m of the camera, rebuilt every frame into 2 batches.
- Haze (every 12th particle, 80 total): camera-right width 1.8 + 0.2*(i%7), up 0.32, colour (0.68,0.49,0.29), alpha 0.28, textured with WindblownDust.texture() (diffuse density), height terrain + 0.3 + 0.12*(i%7).
- Grains (880): 0.012 across x 0.13 along the wind, white x material 0xd5b17c, alpha 0.34.
- Alpha fades by (32 - distance)/8.
- Material: .constant, no depth write, double-sided, WindblownDust modifier.

Pool of 1,600 slots, rebuilt each frame into 2 batched draws (dust quads, clod tetrahedra).
Emission: 22*min(2.5,|v|)*contactLoad per second per contact when |v| > 0.18. Spawn at terrain + 0.018 with tint from track / town / dune / storm-deposit soil colours (+-6%). Dust probability = 1 - (0.25 + 0.42*clayWeight).
Dust particles:
- radius 0.12-0.20, growing x(1 + 0.9*age); life 1.2-1.8 s.
- opacity 0.48 clear / 0.36 storm; fade-in 0.12 s, fade-out over 65% of life.
- velocity damping exp(-1.4 dt), lift +0.045 m/s^2.
- Quad lies in the camera plane, stretched along the projected wind: 1.6x clear, 3.8x storm, by 0.65.
- tint*0.90 + (0.07,0.055,0.035).
Clod particles:
- radius 1.5-3.5 mm plus 6-12 mm*clayWeight; life 0.22-0.38 s + 0.5*clayWeight.
- gravity -9.8, damping exp(-0.7 dt); settle on ground.
Materials:
- Dust: .lambert, 128 squared density texture (plume: pow(envelope,0.65)*pow(noise,0.55)), no depth write, double-sided.
- Clods: PBR white, roughness 1, double-sided, writes depth.
- Both use the WindblownDust modifier: dustTint = vertex colour; diffuse *= pow(tint,2.2); fragment opacity = diffuse.a*tint.a, premultiplied.
Wind advection in storms: dust 1.8/s, clods 0.10/s.

Per racer (4): marks every 6.5 cm per contact. Quad of contact width x 4.2 cm (tracks) or 3.4 cm (tires), at terrain height + 7 mm (town dressing floor blend applies). Vertex colour r = strength (0.24 tracks / 0.19 tires, blending to 0.14 in dunes, x contact load), g = birth storm time.
Material: .constant, blendMode .multiply, double-sided, no depth write, node renderingOrder 10.
- Geometry varyings: strength, born, view distance = length(modelView*pos).
- Surface (#pragma transparent): across = smoothstep(0,0.15,u)*(1 - smoothstep(0.85,1,u)); along = smoothstep(0,0.24,v)*(1 - smoothstep(0.65,1,v)); diffuse = (1 - strength*across*along) grey, alpha 1.
- Fragment (storm only): visibility = exp(-age/10)*(1 - smoothstep(3,65,dist)); colour = mix(white, shade, visibility).
Storage: chunks of 256 marks (1,024 vertices), ring of 128 chunks per racer. Uniforms are written only when they change.

27 plates.
- Frame: SCNBox (w+0.045)x(h+0.045)x0.055, chamfer 0.012; PBR grey 0.17, metal 0.55, roughness 0.65.
- Face: SCNPlane at z +0.029 with a rasterised texture 1024 x round(1024/aspect), aspect 2-9; mip linear, anisotropy 8, roughness 0.82; emission = same texture at intensity 0.12.
- Artwork: background 0x263c3c, accent bar and badge, outline 0xb8aa8c alpha 0.45, title 0xf1e1bc, eyebrow and footer 0xc2b69c, fonts AvenirNextCondensed-DemiBold/Medium with fit-to-box shrinking, 65 enamel-wear specks.
- No shadows; never billboards.

Marvin (positions and normals only, 23 parts): PBR, double-sided.
- shell 0xc3c7c9 metal 0.8 rough 0.65; rubber 0x202a29 r0.88; graphite 0x37403f m0.25 r0.42; steel 0x919b9d m0.7 r0.28; electronics 0x163e36 r0.6; face 0x25282b r0.38; button 0xc83a24 r0.45; hub spokes 0xb4c8c0 m0.5.
- Eyes: SCNShape glyphs, .constant white + emission white, blink by scaling y.
- TrackBelt: 56 shoes per side (SCNBox 0.165x0.008, chamfer 0.001) + ribs 0x2b3432 + 160-segment carcass ring.
R2-D2: shell = Base_Color / Metalness / Roughness / Emission PNG; panels = Barrel_Base / Roughness / Normal, metal 0.15; wheels SCNCylinder 48 segments, rubber 0x555653 r0.94, hub 0x8b969e m0.75 r0.38.
BB-8 / WALL-E: PBR, double-sided; base, normal and emission textures; packed glTF ORM metalRough (B metalness, G roughness, R ambientOcclusion via textureComponents).
All racers get the DirtCoating modifier and castsShadow true.

Start/finish checker: 2x10 SCNBox tiles (chamfer 0.008), 0xddd2b9 / 0x393a32, 4 mm thick at y 0.003. Starting boxes: flat quads 0xe7dcc4 at terrain + 9 mm. Direction arrows: SCNShape 0xd6ba85 at +6 mm. City gate: SCNBox parts, metal 0x60615a (metalness 0.72, r0.79), rusty 0x805443 r0.94, posts SCNCylinder 12 segments. None of the flat decals cast shadows.

- All custom translucent surfaces output premultiplied colour (rgb *= a) under #pragma transparent, with transparencyMode .aOne, writesToDepthBuffer false and depth read on. SceneKit sorts them.
- Trail decals use renderingOrder 10 so they composite after the ground layers (a regression test proves default order hides them).
- The sky uses -10000.
- Overlay stack heights: horizon -0.05, base terrain -0.025, trampled -0.023, patches -0.019, streets -0.016/-0.015, plaza box -0.006..+0.003, pigment +0.0002, trails +0.007. No polygon offset is used.
- Clods are transparent but write depth.

- Material colours: NSColor(srgbRed:) via color(hex).
- Light, fog and ambient tints: NSColor(calibratedRed:) (Generic RGB) holding values computed as linear floats.
- Procedural textures: 8-bit deviceRGB NSBitmapImageRep.
- Vertex palette colours: raw float sRGB bytes/255, converted in shaders with pow(x, 2.2) (an approximation, not the piecewise sRGB EOTF). Trails, drift and storm haze use raw vertex values with no conversion.
- SceneKit linear-space rendering is enabled (no opt-out in Info.plist).

Timer at 1/60 s on the main run loop (.common) drives simulation, scene mutation and camera. Smoke tests use a fixed step of 1/60. dt is clamped to 0.1. An opt-in CADisplayLink at 60 Hz exists (macOS 14+). SceneKit renders continuously at preferredFramesPerSecond 60 on its own thread. The FPS overlay counts didRenderScene callbacks over 0.5 s windows. Requirement: 60 FPS sustained with no drops (the user objected to 58 FPS).
