inventories.quantitative:
Hardware reference: Apple M2 MacBook Air (24 GB), macOS 26.6.2. The drawable is 1920x1080 and the frame budget is 16.67 ms at 60 Hz. Project GPU gate: p99 <= 12.5 ms and maximum < 16.667 ms per minute.

Scene content (10-minute benchmark report):
- Town: 92 cell nodes. 437,850 near / 242,142 far triangles; validate() caps them below 440,000 / 320,000 and fewer than 150 cells.
- 173 exploration cells (51,376 triangles). 497 buildings, 27 signs, 13 streets.
- Crowd: 77 cells, 1,834,674 near / 100,409 far stored triangles. 282 people, of whom 34 walk (up to 10 door residents plus up to 24 street pedestrians).
- Shadow proxies: 92 nodes, 679,992 triangles. Vertices 1,761,272 -> 417,484 and elements 661 -> 338.
- Course surfaces: 5 strips of 768x32 quads, about 245,760 triangles. Desert: 560 tiles of 2,048 triangles at LOD0. Deformable patch: 8,192 triangles each.
- Robots: Marvin 695,172 triangles (plus 112 track-shoe nodes with ribs); R2-D2 25,158; WALL-E 40,158; BB-8 7,166.
- The renderer-study grandstand block alone, with near LOD forced, has 863 meshes and 3,023,194 triangles.

Dynamic effects:
- Debris pool 1,600 particles in 2 draws.
- Storm: 960 particles in 2 draws.
- Trails: 4 racers x up to 128 chunks x 256 marks (up to 131,072 quads). After 10 minutes there were 112,432 quads in 441 nodes before chunking fixes.

Lights and post:
- Lights: 2 directional (shadowed) plus 1 ambient plus IBL.
- Shadow maps 4096 squared and 2048 squared, 116 m wide, 8 PCF samples.
- SSAO prepass at full resolution RGBA16F; SSAO output 960x540 RGBA16F.

GPU frame (Xcode replay of a warm frame, 285 s into a drive):
- 17.39 ms total; 8 render encoders, 4 compute, 67 blit, 2,180 draws.
- Cost shares: dust draw 9.49%, town ground overlay 8.15% (5.35% in the AO-prep encoder), AO prep encoder 20.46%, SSAO compute 9.95%.
- Frozen owned-command-buffer GPU medians: 11.27-11.95 ms; 10.72-10.75 ms with dust hidden; CPU encoding about 2.6-3.2 ms.
- Live Metal HUD: GPU median 13.72 ms, p95 15.43, p99 16.02. Full-city baseline callbacks averaged 59.97/s.

Sustained 10-minute drive: 57.23 FPS mean, live range 40.7-60.3, 1,662 intervals over 25 ms, CPU update p95 2.63 ms. Later runs reached 54.1-56.4 FPS mean, so the current build fails the sustained gate.
- Gate requirements: zero gaps over 25 ms, rolling 10 s rate >= 59.8 FPS, live counter >= 59, msaaSamples 2, shadow widths [2048,4096].

AO input diagnostic prepass: 1.40-1.64 ms. Rejected GTAO prototype: about 7.25 ms.

Memory (renderer study): SceneKit process peak 1,438 MB; Metal allocations peak 2,455 MB.
inventories.validation_existing:
Native smoke tests (AppController command-line modes; each writes PNGs and JSON):
- --smoke-test: sandbox and dirt captures, including native-scene, neck-pan, dirt-grid, dirt-overview/driving/trails/fence, robot close-ups and dirty robots.
- --visual-regression-test: 24-view stationary shadow sweep with world-space shadowed/unshadowed ratio stability. Pass needs >100 repeated samples, each robot >15 shadow samples, and fewer than 1% unstable. MARVIN_SHADOW_AUTO=1 is the negative control. Also renders citizen LOD front/back sheets.
- --binary-sky-smoke-test: 2,000 random skies (separation 1.1-13 deg), light/disc alignment, 3 races, and a sun-occlusion luminance check (>0.6 visible, <0.05 occluded).
- --ground-performance-test, --shadow-culling-test, --mesh-reuse-test: 33 views (11 views x midday, low-sun and storm) at 1920x1080, comparing reference and optimised frames per pixel. Changed fraction above 5/255 must be <0.001, or <0.00001 for strict modes. Includes tangent-reuse fixtures and frustum-classifier checks.
- --trail-material-smoke-test: multiply decal ratios >= 0.65 with hue drift <= 0.04 on sand, clay and dark ground; no re-upload on sub-spacing motion.
- --dust-visibility-test: dust on/off pairs on clay, town and dunes.
- --debris-smoke-test: rendered clod colour via SCNRenderer snapshot, plus grain size and colour per surface.
- --town-smoke-test: 13 named cameras plus robot POV and outer-town detail on/off. Every frame is audited for magenta shader-failure pixels (<20 sampled).
- --navigation-smoke-test: tread impressions visible only with renderingOrder 10 (>100 pixels), including on a raised receiver.
- --sandstorm-smoke-test, --people-smoke-test, --dune-contact-test, --postrace-smoke-test, --town-departure-movie: offscreen 1280x720 frames.
- --display-link-lifecycle-check: FPS overlay is live and passes input through.
- --town-benchmark: 10-minute --city-roam ledger, checked by scripts/rendering/check-sustained-performance.py (the strict gate described in quantitative).
- --benchmark-gpu-probe: LoadedGPUProbe ABBA variants (no-trails, no-sky, no-ssao, no-shadows, front-to-back, constant-ground-pigment, shadow-batch, and others), plus --benchmark-ao-preparation and --benchmark-gpu-capture.

Other harnesses:
- --renderer-study (SceneKit vs RealityKit).
- scripts/rendering: AOPreparationFixture, SceneKitAOFixture, GroundTruthAO with Python checkers; summarize-metal-hud; analyze-frame-timeline; read-game-overview; PresentationCalibration; compare-ao-exports.

The RealityKit study and these fixtures are diagnostics, not acceptance. docs/simulator-agent-rules.md requires visual inspection of the saved images; numeric gates alone are never visual acceptance. The repo already holds many reference captures under the external marvin-town-planning directory, which are the natural 'golden images' for a Windows port.
risks: SceneKit's lighting, shadow PCF, bloom, tone mapping, SSAO and IBL convolution are closed and undocumented. 'Same graphics' can only be reached perceptually by tuning against Mac reference captures, never by porting code. Budget for an image-comparison harness (same camera poses and sun state on both platforms).

Two independently shadowed directional lights with fixed 4096/2048 orthographic maps is unusual. Unity URP shadows only the main light, and several engines force cascades or camera-fitted projections, which reintroduces the shimmer and flicker the project already fixed.

Shader-modifier semantics: view-space _surface data, fragment overrides relative to fog, and geometry modifiers that also run in shadow and SSAO prepasses (animated walker shadows, displaced dune shadows). Engines that do not apply vertex offsets in depth and shadow passes will produce wrong shadows and AO.

Colour pipeline: Generic RGB (calibratedRed) light, fog and sky colours, deviceRGB 8-bit procedural textures, and the pow-2.2 vertex linearisation. Any wrong sRGB/UNORM format choice shifts the whole palette and the dusk and dawn looks the user specifically approved.

Stacked ground overlays a few millimetres apart with no depth writes, sorted by SceneKit and relying on renderingOrder 10 for trails. Different sort keys or depth precision will erase or flicker tread marks and road edges.

Performance is already marginal on M2: GPU 11-16 ms, 2,180 draws, about 3 M triangles in some views, per-frame dynamic mesh uploads, and the full-resolution AO prepass redrawing the scene. The current macOS build fails its own 10-minute 60 FPS gate. A Windows renderer must at least match this and likely needs instancing (crowd, town modules) and GPU-driven particles.
MSAA with HDR: a deferred engine path (HDRP deferred, Unreal deferred) cannot do MSAA. TAA would visibly change thin-geometry and particle appearance.
Crowd vertex animation needs 8 UV channels plus colour and generated tangents. Some engines limit custom vertex streams (Godot) or need special import settings.
Fonts: Avenir Next Condensed (signs) and the macOS system monospaced font (beacon digits) are Apple-licensed and absent on Windows. Text-fit validation and sign legibility depend on them.

Undocumented SceneKit primitive tessellation (SCNBox chamfer, SCNSphere/SCNCylinder segments, SCNText flatness, SCNShape triangulation) makes exact silhouette parity of the sandbox, wheels and gate parts uncertain.
Exploration-detail fading uses SCNNode.opacity, which turns opaque architecture into sorted blended geometry during the fade. Engines will instead dither, pop or need special handling.

The AO restoration investigation showed SceneKit pipeline state is sensitive to shader-modifier changes (restored images differed). Do not rely on per-frame shader swapping semantics when designing the port.

Implicit renderer threading: SceneKit renders presentation copies concurrently while the 60 Hz timer mutates the scene. Windows engines serialise differently, which affects pacing measurements and any uniforms written mid-frame (immutable per-frame textures in DirtCoating and DeformableSand exist for this reason).
open_questions: What are SCNView's runtime colorPixelFormat, depthPixelFormat and stencilPixelFormat for the race view? LoadedGPUProbe records them in loaded-gpu-probe.json, but the artefacts are outside the repo. HDR intermediate format and the MSAA resolve point are also unconfirmed.

What exactly does SceneKit's HDR tone mapping do with defaults (whitePoint, averageGray, min/maxExposure) when wantsHDR is true and exposure adaptation is off? Is the bloom applied before tone mapping? This must be measured empirically, for example by rendering calibrated emissive ramps on the Mac.

Does SceneKit's linear fog actually skip the sky dome, as the shader comment intends, given the fragment modifier writes _output.color directly? Is fog applied to the premultiplied ground overlays and particles?

SceneKit shadow details: PCF kernel, the meaning of shadowRadius (3/2) and shadowSampleCount (8), and the units of shadowBias 0.6 for orthographic directional maps. How does .deferred mode composite shadowColor alpha onto constant-lit materials (menu floor, sandbox)?

How does SceneKit interpret 8-bit deviceRGB NSBitmapImageRep textures (procedural earth, deposit, wear atlas, sky probe) and NSColor calibratedRed constants: sRGB-decoded or linear? This determines numeric parity of the whole palette.
Are the shadow-casting race surfaces, base terrain (castsShadow default true) and deformable patches intended casters, or accidental defaults? It matters for the shadow pass budget on Windows.
Which SceneKit/macOS version's look is the reference (macOS 26.6.2 on M2 per docs)? Should Windows parity be judged against existing marvin-town-planning captures or fresh ones?
Does the Windows port need the diagnostic tooling (LoadedGPUProbe ABBA variants, AO preparation probe, RealityKit study, Metal HUD workflow), or only the smoke and benchmark gates?
What is the target Windows hardware and resolution for the 60 FPS and GPU p99 <= 12.5 ms gate? The current gate is M2-specific.
SCNLevelOfDetail selection: does worldSpaceDistance use node bounds centre or origin, and is there hysteresis? Matching avoids popping differences at the 8/10/24/26/82/130/260 m thresholds.

inventories.overview:
Mos Aster is generated entirely in code at level load (DirtWorld.init -> TownWorld(progress:), run on a GCD worker queue in LevelLoading.swift:54-62). Only surface scans (15 Poly Haven 2K JPGs) and the crowd meshes (crowd.json, exported offline from Blender) are imported; every building, street, prop, ground overlay, sign texture and the plaster wear atlas is procedural.

Generation is deterministic: a 64-bit LCG (citySeed 0xA57E2026, TownWorld.swift:532-536) plus integer index hashes drive a fixed call order (roads -> grandstand -> landmarks -> 3 named venues -> settlement -> infield repair pit -> street life -> market/reference details -> wayfinding -> utilities -> doorstep props -> courts -> 130 household yards -> pedestrian access audit -> ground overlays -> activity placement -> 10 doorway residents + 24 street walkers -> crowd batches -> cell geometry). Inputs are the authored street polylines (13 Hermite-smoothed routes), DirtCourse (track spline projection/height, SimulationCore), TownFootprint (irregular radius ~130 m), InfieldLayout and CityExit reservations. The settlement keeps a protected trackside grid core (<56 m), then grows street-facing compounds by frontage placement and 18,000 dart throws with oriented-box SAT separation, then up to 64 small workshops. A 0.25 m BFS flood grid (TownAccessMap, 1320x1320) audits that every compound gets a reachable doorway (up to 6 replanning iterations that shrink blocks). Result at HEAD: 497 buildings, 492/492 accessible compounds, 282 people, 27 signs.

Geometry is emitted by TownPainter primitives (box, adobe rounded prism with wear UVs/damage cavities, cylinder, dome, beam, cable, cloth, arcade, ring, vessel, crate, doors...) into TownMesh CPU buffers that bake vertex colour x contact shading, world-planar UV0 (x0.48) and a wear-atlas UV1, with up to 4 material slots (plaster/cloth/metal/adobe). Each painter call also appends conservative collision bodies (CityCollisionWorld, 8 m buckets) used by physics, residents, camera clipping and route planning. Meshes are welded (exact attribute + guarded tangent-basis key) and uploaded once as SCNGeometry per spatial cell: 92 architecture cells (16 m core / 32 m outer) with a near/far SCNLevelOfDetail at 82 m, plus 173 near-only 16 m exploration-detail cells that fade in (node.opacity) when the player is in the outer town. Per-frame work is limited to toggling cell shadow casting (75 m radius / 48 m race square, optionally frustum-culled shadow volumes), routing those decisions to welded position-only shadow proxies (TownShadowBatch, categoryBitMask bit 20, on by default since db1be0f), exploration fades, crowd uniforms, and resident navigation.

Materials are SceneKit PBR with Metal shader modifiers: vertex sRGB tint linearised with pow 2.2 and modulated by scan luminance; a 1024^2 procedural wear atlas via SCNMaterial.multiply on UV1; transparent premultiplied ground/street overlays whose alpha comes from vertex colour plus world-space value-noise erosion shaders. Spectators are 12 authored human variants x 3 LODs batched into 77 8-m crowd cells, animated entirely in a geometry shader (head turns, waves, gait) driven by 7 extra UV channels and three shared uniforms. Signs are physical frame+plate nodes with text rasterised once through AppKit (Avenir Next Condensed).

fidelity_spec.feature: TownMesh vertex format and baked shading
fidelity_spec.parameters: Per vertex: position float3 relative to cell centre; normal (flat face normal or analytic smooth normal); UV0 = world-planar projection chosen by dominant |flat normal| axis (Y: (x,z), X: (z,y), else (x,y)) * 0.48; UV1 = wear-atlas coordinate (default 0.0625,0.0625 = neutral tile 0); colour RGBA float = sRGB palette byte/255 * shade, alpha 1 (overlays override alpha). contact = 0.83+0.17*clamp(y/1.2,0,1); shade=(0.94+0.06*max(0,n.y))*contact. Triangles with |cross|^2<=1e-12 dropped. Up to 4 submeshes: slot 0 surface (CityMaterials.plaster), 1 cloth, 2 metal, 3 adobe; empty slots omitted. Indices Int32 triangles, original order kept. Vertex welding key = (position, normal, tangent, bitangent, uv0, uv1, colour) with per-triangle UV-gradient tangent/bitangent; when the normal-projected basis is well-conditioned the directions are quantised to 1/65536 (saves ~10.4% vertices; max merged basis angle 0.001049 deg). No explicit tangents are uploaded: SceneKit generates them for normal mapping.

All PBR. scanned(name): diffuse/normal/rough = Resources/City/<name>-base|normal|rough.jpg (2048^2), wrap repeat, mip linear, maxAnisotropy 4, metalness constant. Geometry modifier: half3 cityTint = pow(max(vertexColor.rgb,0),2.2). Surface: grain=dot(scan.rgb,(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722)); diffuse = tint*(a + b*grain): plaster (0.50, 1.10), adobe (0.60, 1.25), cloth & crowdCloth (0.82, 0.22), metal (0.62, 0.65). Normal intensity: plaster 1.0, adobe 0.85, cloth 0.28, metal 0.55. Metalness: metal 0.55, others 0. Cloth and crowdCloth isDoubleSided. Plaster and adobe: multiply = procedural wear atlas on mappingChannel 1, wrap clamp, mip linear (plaster aniso 4). Skin: white diffuse, roughness 0.64, diffuse = tint; leather: roughness 0.78, diffuse = tint.

1024 x 1024 RGBA8, 8 x 8 tiles of 128 px. Tile index = history*16 + wearSeed%16; history from buildingSeed%100: <30 maintained(0), <70 dusty(1), <92 repaired(2), else neglected(3). Per tile seed=tile*197+31, centerX=0.20+((tile*17)%61)/100, baseHeight=0.12+((tile*13)%24)/100. macro=surfaceNoise(u,v,5,seed), fine=surfaceNoise(u,v,27,seed+17) (periodic value noise, hash 374761393/668265263/1274126177); warp=(macro-.5)*.14+(fine-.5)*.045; base=max(0,1-v/(baseHeight+warp)); level=1 (tile 0) else 0.955+(macro-.5)*.12+(fine-.5)*.035; history>0: level -= base*exposure*(0.65+0.55 macro) with exposure 0.19/0.10/0.30; history 2: superellipse repair patch (radii 0.13+0.022(tile%5), 0.15+0.04(tile%3), cy 0.25+0.12(tile%4), power 4, edge*5) blending to 0.995 or 0.85; history 3: runoff stain exp(-((u-drift)/(0.025+0.035(1-v)))^2)*clamp((v-0.24)*1.6)*(0.65+0.35 fine)*0.21. Output R=level, G=level-(1-level)*0.09, B=level-(1-level)*0.19, each clamped to [0.60,1]. Wall mapping: u along wall bottom edge, v up (flipped), 5% inset per tile; only adobe wall quads (not roofs/props) get wear UVs.

inventories.portable_logic:
Platform-neutral today (only Foundation + simd, no rendering types):
- SimulationCore/CityEscape.swift (131 lines): CityExit geometry, ramp height field, CityGate motor dynamics, CityCollisionWorld spatial buckets. Verbatim-reusable (needs a simd shim if kept in Swift, or a straight C++ translation).
- SimulationCore/InfieldLayout.swift (96): tent origins/yaws, canopy footprints, seeded salvage parts, infield obstacle bodies.
- SimulationCore/TownEscapeRoute.swift (63): grid BFS planner with clearance, line-of-sight simplification, quadratic corner rounding.
- SimulationCore/RaceMapRegion.swift TownFootprint (~10) and DesertTerrain (heightfield used for town floor/dunes).

Algorithmic but currently written against SceneKit value types (SCNVector3/CGPoint containers only) - portable with mechanical type substitution:
- TownWorld.swift layout generation (~1,450 lines: streets/Hermite 243-309, grandstand/landmarks/venues/settlement/door planning/props/yards/courts/access/street life 385-1684), camera clipping math (1703-1778, ~75), statistics/validate (1779-1812, ~35).
- TownPainter (1935-2494, ~560 lines): all primitive tessellation and collision-proxy emission; and TownMesh.triangle (1828-1846) vertex baking. TownMesh.geometry's welding/tangent-key logic (1859-1909, ~50) is portable; only the final SCNGeometry construction (1910-1914, 1921-1929) is SceneKit.
- TownAccessMap.swift (73): BFS flood field and route-to-street - fully pure.
- TownGround.swift mesh building (patch/trampledGround/coveredTerrain geometry ~70 lines); shader strings (~45 lines MSL) need translation.
- TownCrowd.swift: Model JSON decode + union-find arm masks (137-166, ~30), Batch.add per-person posing/variation/mantle (171-239, ~70), CityMaterials.surfaceNoise and plaster wear atlas pixel math (35-91, ~55; output via NSBitmapImageRep).
- CitizenMotion.FootPlacement (102-133, ~30) pure math (reads vertex arrays); the GPU shader (6-82, ~76 lines) is a direct MSL->HLSL translation.
- TownResidents.swift / TownStreetResidents.swift (~450 lines total): scheduling, reservations, yielding, swept collision - ~85% pure, the rest is node transform/uniform writes.
- ShadowVolume.swift (~45): conservative frustum/AABB math (only reads SCNNode/SCNCamera properties at the entry point). Shadow caster policy in TownWorld.updateExplorationDetail (85-108) is pure logic around node flags.
- TownSigns layout math (rects/sizes ~25 lines) is portable; rasterisation is AppKit.
- CityExitWorld apron mesh generation (~45 of 87 lines) is pure.
SceneKit/AppKit-bound and needing reimplementation: SCNGeometry/SCNMaterial/shader-modifier setup (~250 lines across TownWorld/TownGround/TownCrowd/CitizenMotion/TownSigns/CityExitWorld), TownShadowBatch (134, a SceneKit-specific workaround whose concept - depth-only welded position streams - maps naturally to a custom shadow pass), sign text rasterisation (~45), capture harnesses (TownSmoke 328, CityEscapeSmoke 151, TownDepartureMovie 93 - logic portable, IO/render calls not). Precedent: RendererStudy.swift:200-333 already converts town SCNGeometry to an explicit 72-byte vertex layout with computed tangents and re-expresses the CityMaterials tint math in a RealityKit CustomMaterial surface shader.

No test pins an exact layout hash or golden images of the town; visual acceptance has been manual screenshot review.
risks: Layout determinism across platforms: generation relies on threshold tests over libm sin/cos/atan2/hypot results and Float hashing; a 1-ulp difference on Windows (UCRT/MSVC or a different Swift toolchain) can cascade into a different city. If 'same city' is required, either bake the macOS-generated layout/meshes to data or use a correctly-rounded portable math library and add a layout-hash test on both platforms.

SceneKit PBR is a black box: matching the BRDF, image-based lighting from the procedural sky probe, ambient terms, 'multiply' (post-lighting) wear atlas semantics, emission on signs and double-sided cloth lighting requires calibration against reference captures; engine standard materials will look measurably different.

Shader noise portability: fract(sin(dot)*43758.5453) value noise on large world coordinates is GPU/compiler precision dependent; ground pigment, road erosion tongues and dune bands will not be pixel-identical on D3D/Vulkan drivers. Replacing the hash with an integer hash or baked noise texture changes the pattern too.

Tangent space: SceneKit generates tangents implicitly and the welding code was tuned to preserve SceneKit's averaging; a port must generate tangents explicitly (e.g. averaged UV gradients as in RendererStudy, or MikkTSpace) and flip normal-map green for D3D-convention engines, otherwise wall/ground relief lighting shifts.

Transparent overlay ordering: three large coplanar-ish premultiplied layers (trampled ground, doorway patches, streets) plus clay overlays and trail impressions rely on SceneKit's default transparent sort and depth offsets of 2-7 mm; a different sort or depth precision (reversed-Z, different near plane 0.02 m, MSAA resolve) can cause flicker or different blending.

Shadows: the look depends on two single-cascade 116 m orthographic maps (4096/2048) with SceneKit's PCF kernel (sampleCount 8, radius 3/2, bias 0.6), texel snapping and per-cell caster toggling; engine cascaded/virtual shadow maps will change softness and coverage. Dropping the bounded caster policy changes which outer courtyards are shadowed.
Exploration-detail fade uses SceneKit node opacity (transparent rendering of opaque meshes); replicating with dithering or alpha-to-coverage changes the transition look.
Font licensing and text rendering: Avenir Next Condensed is not redistributable; sign textures should be pre-rasterised on macOS or a licensed font obtained; otherwise the 27 signs change.

Performance headroom is already thin on the reference Mac: sustained 10-minute runs fail 60 FPS on M2 (53-57 FPS); GPU p95 ~15.5 ms in short runs. The crowd stores ~1.83M near triangles with 8 UV streams; a naive port (uncompressed 2K textures ~335 MB, double-precision vertex streams, no per-cell culling) could exceed Windows GPU budgets. Target Windows hardware and budgets are not defined.

Construction cost and memory spike: geometry is built on the CPU at every level load (two 1024^2 atlases, 1.32k^2 BFS grid, 27k placement attempts, route planning); a Windows port must keep this off the render thread and may want to cache results.

Shared code coupling: TownMesh and CityMaterials.plaster are also used by the track's brick walls (DirtWorld.swift:268) and TownGround.terrainSurface by the dunes (DesertWorld.swift:12); CityCollisionWorld feeds physics, AI escape routes (PostRaceEscape), audio zones (RaceAudio) and the HUD town map (RaceNavigationMap). Porting this subsystem in isolation will break those consumers.

Behavioural coupling to frame/update cadence: resident throttling uses renderer frustum visibility; gate uses 240 Hz substeps; camera boom smoothing uses exp time constants - any change in update order alters motion slightly.
Half-precision varyings and pow(2.2) (not exact sRGB) tint conversion are part of the look; using hardware sRGB conversion or float varyings shifts colours slightly.
open_questions: Must the Windows build reproduce the exact same city (identical compounds, doors, people) or is a statistically equivalent regeneration acceptable? This decides between baking the layout on macOS versus porting the generator with deterministic math.

Keep the generator in Swift (Swift for Windows + simd shim + Foundation) or translate to C++/engine scripting? The algorithmic code is ~2,500 portable lines but deeply intertwined with SimulationCore physics types.

Which renderer path will own PBR: a custom D3D12/Vulkan renderer reproducing SceneKit's lighting, or an engine (Unreal/Unity/Godot) with calibrated materials? The town's materials, overlays and crowd shader need a programmable surface + vertex stage either way.
How does SceneKit treat the roughness/normal JPGs and the deviceRGB wear-atlas NSImage colour space (sRGB-decoded or linear)? Needs a controlled capture to replicate.
What exact distance metric does SCNLevelOfDetail(worldSpaceDistance:) use (node origin vs bounding sphere centre) - needed to reproduce LOD switch points at 82 m and crowd 10/26 m.

Is the default-on TownShadowBatch (shadow-only welded proxies) a requirement or merely an optimisation that a custom shadow pass makes unnecessary? Its visual equivalence was validated within 5/255 (static views), but moving-camera acceptance was left open.
Should sign textures be shipped pre-rasterised (bit-identical) or rendered on Windows with a licensed/substitute font?
What Windows target hardware, resolution, MSAA level and frame-time budget define 'same graphics' at acceptable performance, given the Mac reference already fails the sustained 60 FPS gate?

Is a pixel-comparison golden-image suite (from the existing 15 town-smoke cameras and the 33-view comparison set) going to be the acceptance mechanism for the port? No golden images are currently checked in.
Should the offline/diagnostic tooling (departure movie, GPU probes, ABBA comparisons, Metal-HUD-based benchmarks) be ported, or replaced by Windows-native equivalents (PIX, RenderDoc, PresentMon)?

inventories.subsystem: Dirt track, desert dunes, terrain and surface effects (DirtWorld + DesertWorld + DirtTrail + DirtCoating + DeformableSand + WindblownDust + SandstormWorld + TrackBelt + FloorGroove; SimulationCore DirtCourse/DesertTerrain/SandDeformation/Sandstorm; Resources/Dirt)
inventories.overview:
DirtWorld (DirtWorld.swift:8) owns one SCNScene for the Dirt Track level. It is constructed on a GCD worker (LevelLoading.swift:55-63), and almost every surface is generated procedurally at load. The race course is a closed periodic cubic B-spline through 16 control points, sampled at 768 points (DirtRace.swift:28-46). The centreline lap is about 136 m and the lane is 3.9 m wide. The elevation function adds a tabletop, rollers, rhythm doubles, a 1.3 m hill, whoops and banking (DirtRace.swift:151-170). From these, courseSurface builds five 768x32 strip meshes: the lane, two berms and two shoulders (DirtWorld.swift:112-126, 435-478). All five share one PBR "clay" material made from the Poly Haven CC0 "dirt" 1K scan, a procedural multiply map and a surface modifier that recolours the clay to rose (DirtWorld.swift:85-108). Other procedural geometry: brick retaining walls batched into two meshes with level bed joints and gate/service cuts (DirtWorld.swift:192-272); heightfield service and city-exit aprons, each with a premultiplied red-clay overlay (DirtWorld.swift:276-372, CityExitWorld.swift:40-85); checker, grid-box and arrow paint; and a baked 768² infield/outfield clay-deposit texture applied in the earth shader in world space (DirtWorld.swift:375-433).

Outside the 156 m town edge, DesertTerrain (SimulationCore) supplies a cached 2 m heightfield. DesertWorld builds 560 static 64 m tiles with crack-free LODs at 0, 130 and 260 m, plus a 4 km horizon plane. TownGround.terrainSurface shades the dune colour, bands and ripple normals in world space. DeformableSand puts opaque 4 m replacement patches (65x65 vertices) where robots touch the dunes. Each patch has a static Metal vertex buffer, and a geometry shader modifier displaces it from an immutable 67x67 R32F height texture that is re-uploaded at 30 Hz from the CPU SandDeformation field. The coarse tile triangles under each patch are removed by rebuilding the tile's index buffer.

Per-frame effects:
- **Tread and tire impressions:** four DirtTrail objects build world-space multiply-blend quads in 256-mark chunks, up to 128 chunk nodes each. They fade in storms through a shader age and distance term.
- **Debris:** a 1,600-slot CPU pool of dust and clods. Its two batched meshes are rebuilt every frame: wind-stretched, view-plane quads with Lambert lighting, and PBR tetrahedra, both premultiplied alpha.
- **Dirt coating on robots:** a geometry-level surface modifier with procedural 3D noise. It is driven by a 2x1 RGBA32F state texture per robot that also carries a dune contact plane.
- **Sandstorm:** about 10% of races. It adds one static drift mesh displaced in the geometry shader by an accumulation uniform, and 960 camera-wrapped grain and haze quads rebuilt per frame. BinarySky switches to dusty linear fog (3-65 m), a muted sky and IBL probe, and suns at 20% intensity.

All weather, deformation, course and terrain maths lives in SimulationCore and is platform-neutral apart from Apple's simd module. All rendering is SceneKit: SCNGeometry, SCNMaterial PBR, shader modifiers written in MSL, LOD, fog, blend modes and rendering order.

platform_dependencies.fidelity_risk: About 11 distinct modifiers rely on SceneKit pipeline semantics that the engine must reproduce. (1) Fog appears to be applied before the fragment modifier: the sky comment says writing _output.color bypasses fog (BinarySky.swift:89), and the trail and drift modifiers overwrite or scale fogged output. (2) The .surface modifier runs before lighting, with _surface.position in view space. (3) The multiply property is applied post-shading. (4) `#pragma transparent` together with transparencyMode .aOne gives premultiplied ONE/INV_SRC_ALPHA blending. (5) Geometry modifiers also run in the shadow passes, so displaced sand patches cast displaced shadows. (6) The interaction between geometry-level modifiers (DirtCoating, DeformableSand) and material-level modifiers. Wrong ordering visibly changes colours, the storm look and decal contrast.

fidelity_spec.parameters: Periodic uniform cubic B-spline over 16 control points (0,-10),(8,-10),(12,-6),(10,0),(5,0),(4,-4),(-1,-4),(-2,3),(6,5),(10,10),(3,12),(-6,10),(-11,5),(-10,-2),(-10,-9),(-5,-10); sampleCount 768; lap about 136.3 m. Half-width 1.95 m, berm 0.35 m, fenceOffset 2.45 m, wall thickness 0.15 m, postHeight 0.40 m. Elevation by phase u: tabletop 0.70 m (u 0.025-0.085, 0.015 ramps); rollers 0.24/0.32/0.24 at u 0.26/0.30/0.34 (half 0.02); rhythm 0.62/0.56 at 0.49/0.54 (half 0.025); hill 1.30 at 0.69 (half 0.095); 6 whoops 0.16 from 0.82 every 0.015 (half 0.0075); base bumps 0.65/0.90/0.55 at 0.17/0.40/0.91 (half 0.065); bank min(0.35,|turn|*3)*(offset/width)². Bump shape h*cos²(t*pi/2). Outer berm crest 0.10 m, inner 0.055 m (sine profile).

5 strip meshes (lane -1.95..1.95 m; outer berm 1.95..2.30 m with sin profile 0.10; inner berm -2.30..-1.95 m with 0.055; two shoulders up to +/-fenceOffset with y=-1 flag meaning ground height). Each 768 segments x 32 strips = 49,152 tris and 25,377 verts. Lane micro-rut 0.0015*sin(across*180+sin(phase*9)*0.8)*sin(across*pi). Normals from neighbour cross products, replaced by height-gradient normals (e=0.025) near the service entry (|x+7.5|<4, -16<z<-9) and the city gate (|gate.x|<6, |gate.y|<2). UV: u=i/768 around the loop, v=(offset+1.95)/3.9 (continuous across lane, berm and shoulder). Nodes cast shadows (SceneKit default).

PBR, base 0x986441, roughness 0.94, double-sided. Diffuse, normal and roughness from Resources/Dirt 1024² JPEGs, wrap repeat, contentsTransform scale (48,1,1): 48 repeats per lap, 1 repeat across 3.9 m. normal.intensity 0.65. multiply = procedural soilTexture(track) 1024x256 at intensity 0.35 (1x per lap). Surface modifier: L = dot(diffuse,(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722)); diffuse = (0.34,0.205,0.145) + L*(0.58,0.44,0.33). Fallback without resources: procedural diffuse plus procedural normal map (soilTexture normal: true).

1024x256 RGBA8. Integer hash n=x*374761393+y*668265263; n=(n^(n>>13))*1274126177; value n^(n>>16) normalised. grain=hash(x,y), blotch=hash(x/16,y/12), groove=sin(v*190+sin(u*pi*12)*0.7), lane=exp(-((v-0.52)/0.27)²). value=(grain-0.5)*0.20+(blotch-0.5)*0.08+groove*0.025-lane*0.13. Track RGB=(0.57+value, 0.37+0.8*value, 0.23+0.55*value). Normal variant: (0.5+(g-g(x+1))*0.22, 0.5+(g-g(y+1))*0.22+cos(v*190)*0.11, 0.97).

fidelity_spec.feature: Earth/ground material and packed earth texture
fidelity_spec.parameters: PBR 0x827656, roughness 1, normal nil. Diffuse = packedEarthTexture 512² (hash grain, CityMaterials.surfaceNoise at 5 and 21 cells, seeds 11 and 31; pebbles where grain>0.984 give -19; RGB 157/140/115 + value). Repeat with contentsTransform 64x over the 256 m plane (4 m tile). Ground mesh = TownGround.coveredTerrain: 64x64 quads of 4 m in 2 elements (shaded; depth-only where 38<=r<=93 m), at y=-0.025.

Surface modifier on the earth copy and the sand material. World p = (inverseViewTransform*_surface.position).xz. Desert mask smoothstep(R-12,R+32,|p|) with R=123+13sin(3a+0.4)+9cos(5a-0.7)+6sin(2a). Dune colour (0.64,0.43,0.23)*(0.83+0.30*grain)+townNoise(p/43)*(0.075,0.058,0.029). Soil = mix(diffuse, townPigment(p)*(1.30+grain), smoothstep(28,42,|p|)), where townPigment uses domain-warped value noise (/31,/37 warp x9; broad /22, fine /5.5; soils (0.255,0.208,0.145) to (0.46,0.36,0.235)). Ripple normal perturbation (0.022*s, 0, 0.008*s)*desert with s=sin(p.x*17+p.y*5.8+1.8sin(p.y*0.41)+sin(p.x*0.22)). Sand material roughness 0.94.

fidelity_spec.feature: Infield/outfield clay deposit (baked decal in earth shader)
fidelity_spec.parameters: 768² RGBA8 premultiplied texture over a 60x60 m world square (UV=(xz+30)/60). Coverage only where course distance > terrainEdge-0.10 (terrainEdge = fenceOffset+0.1+0.45 = 3.0 m). Inside: edge falloff with reach 1.05+0.50sin(19phase)+0.22sin(47phase), service route mask and wheel paths exp(-((lat-0.46)/0.13)²), coverage max(edge*0.78, route*0.73+wheel*0.20). Outside: surfaceNoise macro (23 cells) and detail (79 cells), spread 1.5-3.6 m, pow(falloff,1.65). Alpha clamp 0.94. Colour (184,144,118)+grain*12-6 (minus wheel*15 inside). Shader: constexpr sampler clamp_to_zero, linear, no mips; diffuse = diffuse*(1-a)+rgb.

fidelity_spec.feature: Service embankment and city-exit apron with red-clay overlay
fidelity_spec.parameters: Service: grid (nx<=80)x62 rows, row spacing 0.08 m, extruded from the inner boundary; height = course height minus 0.1 mm smoothstep tuck; skirts down to -0.08 m with a bottom cap; earth copy (identity contentsTransform), UV xz/4; no shadow casting. Exit: 96x100 grid from offset curves fenceOffset+j*0.08, starting at sample 768*0.125-48, tucked 8 mm, skirt to -0.1. Overlay = clay copy using clay UVs (phase, offset mapping) with geometry modifier redSoil=vertex colour r, fragment premultiplied (rgb*=a, a=red); transparencyMode .aOne, no depth write, +0.2 mm offset. Red mask = smoothstep falloffs plus surfaceNoise (7 cells seed 197 / 9 cells seed 327).

Two TownMesh batches with CityMaterials.plaster (scanned plaster PBR; vertex colour sRGB to linear via pow 2.2; diffuse = tint*(0.50+L*1.1); multiply = 1024² wear atlas on UV1 with default UV (0.0625,0.0625), the neutral cell). Brick ~0.43 m (count = ceil(len/0.43)), course 0.13 m, rise 0.124 m (6 mm joint), thickness 0.15 m, running bond (odd rows offset half a step), 4 mm gaps, top inset 5.5% toward centre, 12 mm lip bevel, top-course chips 0-6 mm. Foundation -0.04 m, minimum 3 courses, crest = ground + 0.40 m (outer side uses CityExit.wallTop, ramping to gate height 0.95 m near the gate). Palette 0xa28a70, 0x998068, 0xb0997c, 0x927963, 0xa78c70, 0xb29b80, picked by hash i*73+row*193(+31). Polygon clipping at the gate jamb (half-width 1.68 m) and the service opening (half-width 1.25 m). TownMesh bakes face shade (0.94+0.06*n.y)*(0.83+0.17*min(1,y/1.2)) and planar UV *0.48. 18 tris per brick. Walls cast shadows.

Start/finish checker: 2x10 SCNBox 0.15x0.004x0.39 m (chamfer 8 mm) at y=0.003, 0xddd2b9/0x393a32. Grid boxes: 4 slots x 3 strips (0.025x0.95, 0.86x0.025) at +9 mm, 0xe7dcc4. Arrows: flat chevrons at phases 0.5/1.8/3.5/5.0, 0xd6ba85, +6 mm. None cast shadows. Gate: about 20 boxes (metal 0x60615a metalness 0.72 roughness 0.79; rusty 0x805443 roughness 0.94), 2 cylinder posts r=0.085 with 12 segments, gate 3.2 m wide, 0.95 m high, swung from CityGate.body.

extent 768 m, spacing 2 m (769² cached doubles), townEdge 156 m (flat -0.025 inside). apron=smooth((edge-156)/30), perimeter=smooth((768-edge)/96). Ridge phase (x*0.94+z*0.34+warp)/64 with warp=15(noise(x/90,z/90)-0.5)+7sin(0.019z); asymmetric crest at 0.67; amplitude 6+4*noise(x/127+8, z/113-3); swell 1.8*(0.5+0.5sin((0.3x-0.95z)/29+2noise))². Height -0.025+0.8*apron*perimeter*(amp*ridge+swell). Peak about 9.1 m, max slope about 32.9 deg. Barycentric split along u+v<=1, identical for rendering and collision. Gradient by central difference with e=0.3.

24x24 grid of 64 m tiles minus the central 4x4 (560 tiles). LOD0: 33x33 verts at 2 m, 2,048 tris. LOD1 (stride 2, 130 m): 696 tris. LOD2 (stride 4, 260 m): 280 tris. Boundary cells are fanned so all LODs share the 2 m edge vertices. Normals from DesertTerrain.gradient. UV world/4. No shadow casting; tiles receive shadows. Horizon SCNPlane 4000x4000 m at y=-0.05 with the earth material.

Patch 4x4 m, 65x65 verts (0.0625 m), 8,192 tris, static MTLBuffer (float4 position + float4 normal, stride 32). Base heights are the exact barycentric coarse surface; normals interpolate the coarse vertex normals. Geometry modifier: p=uint2(round(xz*16))+1; y+=h(p); normal=normalize(n+(-dx,0,-dz)*n.y) with dx=(h(p+x)-h(p-x))*8. Height texture R32F 67x67 (1-texel halo from neighbours), nearest filtering, recreated only if a cell changed by >=0.5 mm. Bounding box padded -0.14/+0.11 m. Patches cast shadows and use the dune 'sand' material. Coarse 2 m cells under patches are removed from the tile index buffer; the replacement mesh drops the tile's LODs.

30 Hz (step min(pending,0.05)); only beyond townEdge+8 = 164 m; tiles only where centre is between 160 and 764 m. Capacity 64 tiles; eviction picks the least-recently-touched tile more than 8 m from every robot. Per contact: footprint lateral edge<0.19 m and longitudinal end<0.10 m. Cut zone edge<0.015 and end<0.025: target clamp(sole+0.035-base, -0.12, -0.035*irregular), rate pressure*(1-exp(-18dt)). Banks for edge 0.015-0.19 receive 72% of the removed volume with sin weight; cap +0.095 m. Settling on tiles touched within 2.5 s: flux=((a-b)*0.7+sign*max(0,|slope|-0.04125)*2.2)*dt*loose, loose=clamp((max(a,b)+0.004)/0.045). Contacts: Marvin and WALL-E tracks (length max(|z|*2, halfDepth*1.8)), R2-D2 3 wheels, BB-8 1, min width 0.10, length 0.12. Penetration weight clamp((pen+0.025)/0.05) scales trails and dust.

One trail per racer: [tracks (Marvin), tires (R2-D2, 3 contacts), tires (BB-8, 1), tracks (WALL-E)]. Mark every 0.065 m of travel per contact, heading slerped, skipped when not in dirt contact or on a teleport (>2 m). Quad width = contact width; length 0.042 m (tracks, so dashed) or 0.0689 m (tires, overlapping). Height terrain(+storm,+sand)+0.007 m (town floor clamp max(ground,0) below 154 m). Normal from terrain gradient (e=0.04). Strength tracks 0.24 / tires 0.19 on town and clay, 0.14 on dunes (30 m blend past 156 m), times sand contact weight. Vertex colour r=strength, g=birth time. Material constant lighting, blendMode .multiply, double-sided, no depth write, renderingOrder 10, no shadows. Surface: shade = 1 - s*across*along with across=smoothstep(0,0.15,u)*(1-smoothstep(0.85,1,u)), along=smoothstep(0,0.24,v)*(1-smoothstep(0.65,1,v)). Storm fragment: vis=exp(-age/10)*(1-smoothstep(3,65,viewDist)); output = mix(1, shade, vis). Chunks of 256 marks (1,024 verts), ring of 128 chunks per trail.

Pool 1,600 ring slots. Emission per contact = dt*min(2.5,|wheel speed|)*22*contactLoad per second (55/s max per contact; 8 contacts in total, so up to 440/s), when speed>0.18, not in collision and in dirt contact. Tracked robots emit at the trailing end (|z|>=halfDepth*0.85). Spawn y = terrain+0.018. Tint blends town (0.62,0.55,0.45), clay (0.64,0.43,0.31) within width+0.7 m of the course, dune sand (0.78,0.57,0.34) via smoothstep 156-192 m, and storm-deposit cover; random *(0.94-1.06). Dust probability 1-(0.25+0.42*clayWeight); dust tint *0.90+(0.07,0.055,0.035). Dust: radius 0.12-0.20 m growing *(1+0.9*age), life 1.2-1.8 s, vy0 0.30-0.55*sqrt(kick), drag exp(-1.4dt), lift +0.045 m/s², fade in 0.12 s, fade out over 65% of life, opacity 0.48 clear / 0.36 storm. Clods: radius 1.5-3.5 mm + clayWeight*6-12 mm, life 0.22-0.38 s + 0.5*clayWeight, gravity -9.8, drag exp(-0.7dt), extra back kick 0.35*clayWeight, ground stop (life capped at 0.09 s), fade 0.025/0.12 s, opacity 0.70. Storm: velocity relaxes toward wind at rate 1.8 (dust) or 0.10 (clods). Ground = storm height + sand offset.

2 batched meshes rebuilt every frame. Dust: view-plane quads (normal = camera back vector) of half-extent radius*stretch along the projected wind (stretch 3.8 in storm, 1.6 clear; falls back to the camera right axis) and radius*0.65 across. Material lightingModel .lambert, diffuse = 128² plume texture (white, alpha = pow(envelope,0.65)*pow(noise,0.55), envelope = (sin(pi u)sin(pi v))², noise from surfaceNoise at 5 and 17 cells), double-sided, no depth write. Clods: 4-vertex tetrahedron (4 tris) of the clod radius with radial normals; PBR white roughness 1, depth-writing. Both use WindblownDust: vertex tint^2.2 multiplies diffuse; fragment premultiplied (rgb*=a, a=tex.a*vertex.a); `#pragma transparent`. No per-particle sorting; no shadow casting.

Geometry-level .surface modifier on every visible non-constant part (CAD parts without UVs get a zero UV stream). Uniforms: dirtToBody (part to robot root), dirtHeight, dirtWheelX (Marvin 0.262225, R2 0.213, WALL-E |contact.x|, BB-8 0), dirtRolling (BB-8 'ball:' and 'link:' parts). State texture 2x1 RGBA32F: texel0 = sand plane (gx,gz,intercept,active), texel1.r = amount. Amount += travel/75 m while in dirt contact (max 1), quantised to 1/32, reset on new race. Shader: p = body-space pos/height; low = 1-smoothstep(0.08,0.58,p.y) (or 1 if rolling); nearWheel = exp(-((|p.x|-wheelX)*9)²); rear = 1-smoothstep(-0.22,0.24,p.z); patches = valueNoise(p*28); specks = smoothstep(0.58,0.76,noise(p*145)); splash = smoothstep(0.38,0.68,patches)*low*(0.45+0.35nearWheel+0.20rear); dust = (0.04+0.22low)*(0.55+0.45patches); coverage = clamp(amount*(dust+0.85splash+0.40specks*low), 0, 0.92); soil = mix((0.19,0.105,0.045),(0.42,0.29,0.16),patches). diffuse mixed toward soil, roughness toward 1, metalness and selfIllumination scaled by (1-c). Dune rim (in sand): world plane height, grain = noise(world*130), rim = (1-smoothstep(-0.004,0.035,y-plane+(grain-0.5)*0.016)); sand (0.64,0.43,0.23)*(0.84+0.25grain) mixed at 0.88, roughness 0.96. Plane refit at 30 Hz with e=0.35 m. Noise hash fract(sin(dot(p,(127.1,311.7,74.7)))*43758.5453) with trilinear smoothstep.

Independent 10% chance per race and per Cmd-R. Advanced on the 240 Hz physics clock. accumulation = min(1, 0.18+elapsed/180). Wind gust = 19+4sin(0.47t+0.013x)+2sin(1.13t+0.02z) m/s, direction angle 0.65+0.09sin(0.21t). 17 drifts centred on the course (offsets -0.72/0/+0.72) with along 0.75-1.29 m, across 1.1-2.18 m, height 0.065-0.145 m; profile h*(1-r)²*(1+0.3u) in a frame rotated (0.796,0.605) with sinusoidal warps; zero beyond |x|,|z|>=24. Drag 0.5*1.1*0.55*area*|v_rel|v_rel/mass.

Static, about 9,234 independent quads (0.10 m grid over +/-23.2 m wherever the deposit exceeds 1e-5), so about 18.5k tris and 36.9k verts. y = DirtCourse.height+0.002. Vertex colour = (deposit, d/dx, d/dz, 1). Geometry modifier: depth = color.r*deposition (uniform = accumulation), y += depth, normal perturbed by the slopes. Surface: diffuse (0.57,0.38,0.23)*(0.82+0.5*grain) where grain = mean RGB of the packed earth texture at UV xz/2 (repeat). Fragment: discard if depth<0.0004; coverage smoothstep(0.0004,0.025,depth), premultiplied. PBR roughness 1, no shadow casting.

960 particles in deterministic initial positions; every 12th is haze (80), the rest grains (880). Advected by the wind sampled at the camera position. Wrapped to +/-32 m around the camera in x/z. Haze y = course height+0.3+(i%7)*0.12; grains re-seeded within eye.y-6..+10 when more than 10 m away vertically. Grains: streak quad half 0.012 m along camera right by 0.13 m along the wind; colour material 0xd5b17c; alpha 0.34*clamp((32-d)/8). Haze: camera-aligned quad half-width 1.8-3.0 m by 0.32 m half-height; vertex colour (0.68,0.49,0.29); diffuse = 128² non-plume WindblownDust texture; alpha 0.28*fade. Constant lighting, double-sided, no depth write, WindblownDust premultiplied shader. 2 meshes rebuilt every frame.

Storm: fog 0xae865b linear 3-65 m (clear: horizon colour, 115-240 m). Sun intensities 1550/470 scaled by 0.20. Ambient 0xd4b48a at intensity 320 (clear 260-70*day, colour (0.54,0.62,0.78)). IBL probe from zenith (0.46,0.34,0.23) and horizon (0.68,0.50,0.32) at intensity 0.75. Sky fragment output = mix(sky, stormTint (0.46,0.29,0.14)+0.025*sky, 0.97). Town hides weather nodes and most people (TownWorld.setStorm). Dome: SCNSphere r=220, 48 segments, front-face culled, no depth read or write, renderingOrder -10000.

Per side: 56 shoes (SCNBox 0.165324 x 0.008 x pitch*0.80, chamfer 1 mm, rubber material) plus 56 ribs (0.38w x 0.003 x 0.42pitch, 0x2b3432 roughness 0.95, offset alternately +/-0.23w; a new material instance per rib). pitch = circumference/56 = 1.61082/56 = 0.02877 m. Carcass ring: 160 segments x 4 faces, 1,280 tris, inset 4-13 mm. Each frame the shoes are positioned from TrackLoop.sample(travel+i*pitch) (radius 0.11935, centreY 0.12485, rear -0.24152, front 0.18894).

V-channel annulus, inner radius 0.522 m, centre 0.54 m, outer 0.558 m, depth 0.012 m; 2 bands x 128 segments (512 tris); flat normals per band; material 0x70583f roughness 0.95; one per checkpoint (5). Not used on the Dirt Track.

Main tick 60 Hz Timer (optional CADisplayLink); physics 240 Hz substeps; DirtWorld.update(dt) each tick with dt clamped to 0.1 s and 0 when paused. Sand field 30 Hz. Coating sand plane 30 Hz. Shadow centre snapped to light-space texels (116/mapSize). Dirt Track camera: zFar 250, FOV 48 deg, HDR on, bloom 0.38/1.2/12, SSAO 0.70/1.6/0.025, MSAA 2x (the sandbox uses 4x).

inventories.portable_logic:
Pure SimulationCore (Foundation plus SIMD types; it needs a shim only for Apple's `simd` functions such as simd_normalize, simd_length, simd_distance and simd_quatd) can be reused verbatim with the Swift toolchain on Windows, or translated mechanically:
- DirtRace.swift, 327 lines: DirtCourse B-spline, offset-curve trimming, a 768-sample projection BVH that is exact against an exhaustive oracle, elevation, jumps and banking, berm, shoulder and service heights, resolveMove, traction, lap counting, scores, standings.
- DesertTerrain.swift, 59 lines: deterministic heightfield, hash noise, barycentric sampling, gradient.
- SandDeformation.swift, 191 lines: tile cache, stamp, banks, settling, snapshots with halo, contact weight.
- Sandstorm.swift, 63 lines: weather draw, wind, 17 drifts, deposit field, drag.
- TrackLoop.swift, 24 lines.
- CourseLayout.swift, 57 lines.
- CityExit in CityEscape.swift, about 75 relevant lines: gate frame, wallTop, rampHeight.
- Simulation.terrainHeight, supportHeight, hasDirtContact and duneOrientation, about 15 lines.

Algorithmic but SceneKit-typed code inside MarvinSimulator. It uses SCNVector3, CGPoint, SCNGeometry and NSBitmapImageRep only as containers, so it is reusable after swapping the types. Roughly:
- courseSurface strip generation, about 45 lines (DirtWorld.swift:435-478).
- Brick wall generation with jamb clipping, about 80 (DirtWorld.swift:192-272).
- Service embankment heightfield, skirt and red mask, about 95 (DirtWorld.swift:276-372).
- Infield deposit bake, about 60 (DirtWorld.swift:375-421).
- Packed earth, soil and dust texture bakers, about 60 (DirtWorld.swift:48-64,479-504; WindblownDust.swift:24-40), plus CityMaterials.surfaceNoise, 11 lines.
- Paint and grid layout, about 35 (DirtWorld.swift:132-166).
- City exit apron, about 45 (CityExitWorld.swift:40-85).
- Dune tile LOD stitching, about 50 (DesertWorld.swift:17-57).
- Patch construction, hole-index rebuild and the 30 Hz scheduler, about 90 (DeformableSand.swift:15-97).
- Debris particle simulation, emission rules and the batch vertex builder, about 150 (DirtWorld.swift:520-671).
- DirtTrail mark generation and chunk ring, about 80 (DirtTrail.swift:83-163).
- DirtCoating amount and plane fit, about 22 (DirtCoating.swift:41-62).
- Storm drift mesh and particle advection/recycling, about 90 (SandstormWorld.swift:41-112).
- TrackBelt carcass and shoe placement, about 50.
- FloorGroove, about 25.
- BinaryDaylight sun-direction and extinction maths, about 40 (BinarySky.swift:8-28,154-170).
In total about 1,050 lines of algorithmic code.

Shader logic: about 160 lines of MSL in 11 modifiers. The maths (value-noise hashes, smoothsteps, premultiply, displacement) translates line-for-line to HLSL, GLSL, WGSL or Godot shading language. The integration points (_surface, _geometry, scn_frame, fog order) must be re-plumbed.

Not reusable: SCNScene, SCNNode and SCNMaterial wiring, MTL resource creation, NSImage, SCNLevelOfDetail, fog and light APIs, and the SCNRenderer-based smoke harnesses.
inventories.quantitative:
All counts are computed from the code. Lap, wall and drift figures were estimated with a Python port of the course maths.

Static geometry:
- Course strips: 5 meshes x 49,152 tris = 245,760 tris and 126,885 verts. They cast shadows.
- Lap centreline: about 136.3 m. Inner and outer wall boundaries: about 120.3 m and 152.1 m, i.e. about 280 and 354 brick columns, about 1,900 and 2,600 bricks, roughly 34k and 46k tris (18 tris per brick). That gives 2 draw calls plus shadow passes.
- Service embankment: up to 80x62 cells, about 9.9k tris plus skirt, drawn twice (base and overlay).
- City exit apron: 96x100 cells, 19,200 tris plus about 1.2k skirt, drawn twice.
- Ground plane: 8,192 tris in 2 elements.
- Dune tiles: 560 nodes. Per tile, LOD0 2,048 tris and 1,089 verts; LOD1 696 tris; LOD2 280 tris. LOD0 for all tiles would be 1.15M tris, but zFar 250 m and fog culling limit what is visible.
- Horizon: 1 quad.
- Sky dome: SCNSphere with 48 segments.
- Storm drift mesh: about 9,234 quads, 18.5k tris, 36.9k verts. Hidden when there is no storm.
- Paint: 20 chamfered boxes, 4 grid nodes, 4 arrows.
- Gate: about 20 boxes and 2 cylinders.
- Marvin belts: 2 x (56 shoes + 56 ribs) = 224 small box nodes and 2 x 1,280-tri carcasses. All 112 shoe transforms are updated every frame.

Dynamic geometry:
- Debris: pool of 1,600; at most 440 particles/s (8 contacts x 55/s). 2 draw calls; up to about 6.4k verts (48 B each, about 307 KB) rebuilt every frame.
- Storm particles: 960 quads (880 grains and 80 haze) in 2 draws, 3,840 verts rebuilt every frame.
- Trails: 4 trails x 128 chunks x 256 marks gives at most 131,072 quads, 262k tris and 512 nodes or draws. A 3-lap race is roughly Marvin 12.6k marks, R2 18.9k, BB-8 6.3k and WALL-E 12.6k (2 contacts each, every 0.065 m). The current chunk is re-uploaded (up to 1,024 verts x 48 B) every frame while moving. Measured during a 10-minute town drive: 25,302 quads / 101 nodes after 1 minute, growing to 112,432 quads / 441 nodes (sustained-fix/plan.md:35-37). Hiding trails did not restore 60 FPS.
- Sand patches: at most 64 x (4,225 verts, 8,192 tris) = 524k tris. Each patch is its own draw and casts shadows. A 67x67x4 B = 18 KB texture is uploaded per dirty patch at at most 30 Hz. The stress fixture reached 47 patches; the cache test forced 324 allocations.
- Coating: 4 robots x 32 B texture at at most 30 Hz.

GPU and CPU timing (Apple M2, 24 GB, 1920x1080; SceneKit callback cadence, not presentation):
- Dune route, 45 s: 59.99 callbacks/s, p95 interval 18.18 ms, p95 CPU update 5.57 ms.
- Four robots deforming dunes, 30 s: 60.00/s, p95 22.55 ms, 1 interval over 25 ms, p95 CPU 8.37 ms.
- Storm vs clear: 59.977 vs 59.975/s; CPU p95 1.70 vs 1.01 ms.
- Dust lift: 59.975/s, CPU p95 1.19 ms.
- Xcode replay of a warm frame: 17.39 ms, 2,180 draws. The dust draw (1,506 indices) took 9.49% of GPU time; hiding dust cut the GPU median from 11.74-11.90 ms to 10.72-10.75 ms (apple-gpu-profiling.md:195-204).
- The GPU p95 budget had less than 1 ms headroom at 60 Hz in earlier passes (GPU p95 about 15.5-15.7 ms).

Particle and visual parameters:
- Dust texture mean alpha 15% (earlier 6.6%); clear opacity 0.48, about 7.2% mean initial coverage.
- Dust life 1.2-1.8 s; clod life 0.22-0.88 s.
- Deformation bounds: cut down to -0.12 m, bank up to +0.095 m. Stress run: 3.49 cm compaction, 2.14 cm banks.
- Shadow maps: 4096² for sun 1 and 2048² for sun 2 in code. The docs say 2048/1024, which is stale.
inventories.validation_existing:
SimulationChecks executable (Tests/SimulationCoreTests, a SwiftPM executableTarget):
- testSandstorm: 10,000 seeded draws must give 900-1,100 storms with consecutive storms possible. Clear weather is inert. Depth must grow 4x after 180 s. The rendered 10 cm drift triangulation must stay within 5 mm of the analytic depth. Player positions must be identical at 30, 60 and 120 Hz.
- testDesertTerrain: town flat at -0.025, render/collision barycentric agreement to 1e-10, no seams, peak above 8 m, slope below 0.67, all four chassis climb a dune.
- testSandDeformation: cuts below -1 cm and banks above 5 mm with finite bounds, exact tile-edge continuity, the GPU 67x67 snapshot must equal the collision sampler exactly, quaternion orthogonality, cache eviction with a protected robot (capacity 64, more than 128 allocations), reset.
- testExactCourseProjection: BVH vs exhaustive scan over 24,499 queries.
- ServiceAccessChecks and others cover course geometry used here.

Native smoke tests (packaged app flags, App.swift:92 and 239-269):
- --debris-smoke-test (DirtWorld.checkDebris + checkClodRendering): emission on clay, town and dunes; grain size clay > 3x dunes; dune tint lighter by more than 0.08; contact heights exact; batch colours present; pause, stop, expiry and reset; rendered clod pixel colours.
- --trail-material-smoke-test: on sand, clay and dark ground, more than 100 changed pixels and no pixel darker than a 0.65 ratio or with a hue spread above 0.04. No upload on sub-spacing motion. The storm uniform updates without a geometry upload.
- Full-race trails, part of the main smoke at App.swift:1134: no missing marks while grounded, no airborne marks, no buried marks against hitTestWithSegment on the lane mesh, more than 500 samples.
- --dust-visibility-test: dust on/off image pairs at 1280x800 on 3 surfaces. The pass gate checks emission only; the images need manual review.
- --dune-contact-test: four robots, 30 s script, photos, coating on/off pixel delta near WALL-E's running gear, opaque Marvin body pixels, patch cap, finite bounds, pause and reset. Variants MARVIN_DUNE_LIVE and MARVIN_DUNE_MOVIE.
- --sandstorm-smoke-test: full storm race, captures, floor penetration below 3 mm, drift depth above 2.5 cm, head- vs tailwind, shelter, population. Optional MARVIN_STORM_MOVIE.
- --weather-reset-test: Cmd-R draws.
- --storm-race-test: all 24 grid permutations finish without BB-8 escaping.
- --ground-performance-test: 11 views x 3 lighting setups at 1920x1080, reference vs optimised, changed fraction below 0.001.
- --binary-sky-smoke-test.
- --town-benchmark [--dune-roam] with MARVIN_SANDSTORM=1, plus diagnostic flags --benchmark-no-deformation, --benchmark-no-contact-coating, --benchmark-no-sand-shadows, --benchmark-transparent-ground.

Rendering scripts in /Users/m1/marvin/scripts/rendering (sustained performance, Metal HUD) are macOS-specific.

The docs/simulator-agent-rules.md acceptance matrix requires rendered images with and without effects, plus manual review of trails, dust, dune contact and storm. Pixel thresholds are SceneKit-calibrated and would need re-baselining.
risks: Shader-modifier semantics are the main fidelity risk. Eleven MSL modifiers depend on SceneKit-specific order. Fog appears to be applied before the fragment modifier (BinarySky.swift:89 says writing _output.color bypasses fog), multiply is applied post-lighting, the .surface stage runs pre-lighting with view-space _surface.position, and `#pragma transparent` gives premultiplied output. Small ordering differences change the storm look, trail contrast and overlay colours.

SceneKit's PBR BRDF and IBL from a 64x32 probe are undocumented. Clay, dune and brick tones were art-directed by the user ('rose clay distinct from yellow sand'; a dark track was rejected), and engine standard-lit materials will not match without tuning or a custom BRDF.

Two shadowed directional suns: Unity URP cannot shadow a second directional light, so that engine choice would need HDRP or a custom renderer. Forward-shadow receipt on transparent overlays (drift mesh, red-soil overlay, Lambert dust) is often unsupported or different in deferred renderers.

Multiply-blended tread decals (no depth write, renderingOrder 10, drawn after town ground decals) map poorly onto deferred DBuffer decals, which apply before lighting. They need a forward translucent modulate pass to keep the 'multiply the lit surface' behaviour that the trail pixel tests verify.

Vertex displacement (sand patches, storm drifts) must also run in the shadow and depth prepasses and use integer texel loads with the 1-texel halo. Otherwise shadows or SSAO detach from the visible ruts, or ruts shift by half a cell.

MSAA 2x vs TAA: deferred engines push toward TAA, which smears the per-frame-rebuilt, wind-stretched dust quads and the thin brick joints and trail edges. Adding a velocity buffer for fully procedural per-frame meshes is extra work.

Performance patterns that are cheap in SceneKit may not be elsewhere (and the reverse). Several meshes are rebuilt from scratch every frame (debris, storm particles, the current trail chunk), up to 512 trail chunk nodes accumulate (112k quads after 10 minutes), and there are up to 64 patch draws plus shadows and 224 belt-shoe nodes per Marvin with per-rib materials. The existing M2 GPU budget already had less than 1 ms headroom.
Hole-punched dune tiles drop their LODs (DeformableSand.swift:91-92). A faithful port must decide whether to reproduce this quirk.

Load-time CPU cost (O(N²) offset-curve trimming 33 times per strip, a 590k-projection deposit bake, about 1.5M triangles of terrain generation, several MB of procedural textures) currently runs on a GCD worker. Engines that require main-thread object creation need the CPU and GPU halves split.

Colour-space handling of procedural NSBitmapImageRep textures (deviceRGB) and mixed NSColor constructors (srgbRed in material(), calibratedRed in BinarySky) must be reproduced exactly when deciding sRGB vs linear, or hues will shift.

Double-precision simulation: moving SimulationCore to float types (e.g. Unity Vector3) would break the exact-equality validations (GPU snapshot equals collision sampler, projection oracle) and could change deformation results.
Debris uses the system RNG (Double.random), so the visuals are not reproducible frame-for-frame. Pixel-diff validation of the port can only be statistical for dust and clods.

Engine particle systems such as Niagara, the VFX Graph or GPUParticles may sort, light or billboard differently. The current behaviour is view-plane-aligned, wind-stretched, unsorted within a batch, Lambert-lit with camera-facing normals, premultiplied, with sRGB-to-linear vertex tint. Reproducing it is easiest with custom dynamic meshes.
open_questions: Does SceneKit apply scene fog before or after the .fragment shader modifier for all lighting models? The sky comment implies the modifier can override fog. This must be verified, for example with a capture, because trails (multiply), dust (premultiplied) and drifts depend on it.

When a geometry-level .surface modifier (DirtCoating, DeformableSand's .geometry modifier) coexists with material-level modifiers, which wins or how do they compose in SceneKit? Do any imported racer materials carry their own .surface modifiers? AOMaterialBinding.swift:21-26 explicitly guards against both being present.

What are the SceneKit default sampler settings (mipFilter, maxAnisotropy) for the clay and earth textures, which do not set them, and how does SceneKit generate mipmaps? A frame capture is needed to replicate grazing-angle appearance of the 48x-repeated clay.
Does SceneKit's .lambert lighting model use scene.lightingEnvironment, and how is lighting applied to the double-sided, camera-plane dust quads (are normals flipped on back faces)?
Do the shadow map sizes (4096/2048 in BinarySky.swift:100) or the docs (2048/1024 in dirt-city.md) represent the intended production configuration?
Is the loss of dune-tile LODs after hole punching (DeformableSand.swift:91-92) intentional, and should a port reproduce it?

Should the poly-haven normal map's OpenGL convention be confirmed against SceneKit's tangent-space convention? This determines whether a D3D-convention engine needs a green flip or the Poly Haven DX variant.
Should procedural textures be baked offline for the port, which needs bit-exact hash behaviour (UInt32 wrapping) in the generator language, or generated at runtime as today?

What is the exact SceneKit transparent draw order between the dust batch, clod batch, storm haze/grains, red-soil overlays, town ground decals and trails? Only trails (10) and sky (-10000) set renderingOrder explicitly; the rest rely on SceneKit's per-node depth sort.

Is Swift-on-Windows reuse of SimulationCore desired? If so, a simd shim must cover simd_quatd, simd_double3x3, simd_normalize, simd_length, simd_distance, simd_dot and simd_cross for the 13 SimulationCore files that import simd.

inventories.subsystem: Robots/characters (Marvin CAD assembly, R2-D2, BB-8, WALL-E), procedural animation and race "acting", town crowds and walking residents, and the offline asset pipeline
files_read: Python inspection (read-only) of Resources/Marvin/geometry.bin, R2D2/mesh.json, BB8|WallE/Generated/mesh.json, City/crowd.json, BB8|WallE/source.glb JSON chunks, R2D2 source zips; sips texture dimensions
inventories.overview:
Each of the four racers is one shared object: Robot (Marvin), R2D2, and ImportedRacer(.bb8/.wallE). All are built at launch in App.swift:103-106 from Bundle.main.resourceURL. The same node trees are reparented between the menu portrait SCNScene, the sandbox World scene and the DirtWorld scene (App.swift:112,458,475-476,517-519; MainMenu.swift:197-202). There are no clones, except in the visual-regression capture.

No model is loaded with SCNScene(url:), ModelIO, glTF, USD or RealityKit. Offline Python converts every source into a custom format, and Swift builds SCNGeometry by hand:
- Marvin: a packed little-endian geometry.bin plus manifest.json. Each part has interleaved float32 position+normal (stride 24) followed by uint32 triangle indices.
- R2-D2, BB-8 and WALL-E: verbose JSON (positions, normals, texcoords, indices, material index, pivots). WALL-E also carries 253 4x4 frames per tread link.
- Crowd: crowd.json holds 12 variants x 3 LODs, with 9 floats per vertex including a semantic surface id.

There is no skinning, morphing, SCNAction, CAAnimation or keyframe playback at runtime. All robot motion is procedural node transforms, set each frame from SimulationCore state (signed left/right track travel, rollingTravel, heading, bodyPitch/bodyRoll or the duneOrientation quaternion, head yaw/pitch, elapsed):
- Marvin: a two-node yaw/pitch neck rig at CAD pivots, gated by an SAT clearance test (HeadClearance). Treads are 56 animated shoes per side on an analytic stadium loop (TrackLoop), plus spinning hub markers and blinking emissive eye strokes.
- R2-D2: three added procedural rollers, and a dome that swivels about an inclined axis.
- BB-8: the shell orientation is integrated as no-slip rolling from ground displacement. The head rides on a mount at the ball centre.
- WALL-E: the authored tread animation is resampled offline into 253 rigid frames per link and scrubbed at runtime by travel/beltLength with lerp+slerp. Gears spin by travel/radius, and the arms are pivot nodes.
- Race "acting" (RacePerformance, pure Swift) outputs a Pose (yaw, pitch, roll, arms, focus) that is added on top of manual input.

Crowds: TownCrowd pre-poses static people on the CPU into 8 m cell batches, with a per-person palette in vertex colours and three LODs. All limb motion (head scans, torso turns, waves, walking gait) runs in a SceneKit .geometry shader modifier (CitizenMotion). It reads per-vertex bind frames and joint weights from seven extra texcoord channels, so it is hand-written GPU rigid-segment deformation. There are 10 doorway visitors (TownResidents) and 24 street walkers (TownStreetResidents). Each is an individual node with its own material copies, whose uniforms (crowdTime, walkCycle, walkBlend) drive a gait based on distance walked. A CPU copy of the same leg transforms (FootPlacement) keeps the soles grounded. Navigation, swept collision, door scheduling and off-screen throttling run on the CPU.

Pipeline: build-app.sh runs prepare-simulator-assets.py, which hash-stamps inputs and outputs in .build/asset-cache and only re-runs exporters when something changed. The three robot exporters use only the Python standard library. Only the offline crowd exporter needs Blender 4.5 LTS (bpy). The shipped crowd.json is committed through Git LFS. Nothing in the pipeline is macOS-only; only the build and packaging shell script is.

platform_dependencies.fidelity_risk:
SceneKit's PBR BRDF, split-sum IBL from scene.lightingEnvironment, ambient-light handling (menu stage uses ambient 650 plus directional 1100 with no IBL) and emission/multiply composition are undocumented and differ from Filament, Unity and Unreal. Several quirks must be reproduced rather than corrected:
- A texture replaces the scalar instead of multiplying it (WALL-E metallicFactor 0.883 is ignored where the ORM texture exists).
- WALL-E's glTF linear baseColorFactor is fed in as sRGB through NSColor(srgbRed:).
- BB-8's specular-glossiness texture is dropped, and constant metal 0.2 / rough 0.5 are used.
- WALL-E eye glass has alpha 0.853; KHR_materials_transmission and KHR_materials_specular are ignored.
- R2-D2 materials are single-sided; all others are double-sided.
- Normal maps use the OpenGL +Y convention, so green must be flipped for DirectX-convention engines.
- Unknown: whether SceneKit sRGB-decodes grayscale or 4-bit roughness/metalness PNGs.
