inventories.overview:
Validation is compiled into the shipping binary. MarvinSimulator scans argv for one of 29 mode flags followed by an output directory (App.swift:90-94, smokeDirectory). When set, weather is forced clear (App.swift:97), the 1/60 s Foundation Timer is used instead of a display link (App.swift:171-181), and the simulation advances with a fixed 1/60 step regardless of wall time or focus (App.swift:421-423). On the 20th main-menu tick, tick() dispatches to a check function (App.swift:231-333) that drives the real AppController/DirtWorld/TownWorld/RaceAudio objects synchronously, often simulating 10-30 minutes of game time without real-time rendering, saves PNG/JPEG/WAV/JSON into the directory and calls exit(0|1). --smoke-test runs the menu checks and then a composite race smoke at frame 150 (App.swift:787-1157) that writes smoke.json. Input is injected as synthesized NSEvents using macOS virtual key codes.

Visual assertions compare the build against itself. The same frozen state is rendered twice with one feature toggled (shadows, dust, coating, reference vs optimized mesh) and compared per pixel through NSBitmapImageRep. Other checks are a magenta shader-error audit on every saved town frame, luminance probes and world-space projected sampling. No golden or reference images are stored or diffed across builds. The rules require humans, plus an 'independent Codex Astra judge', to inspect the saved images.

Performance: --town-benchmark runs in real time in a 960x540-point window (a 1920x1080 drawable on a 2x display). TownFrameMeter records SCNSceneRendererDelegate didRenderScene wall-clock intervals, FrameRateHUD records the live counter, and the run writes benchmark.json, timeline.json, resources.json, displayed-fps.json and final-fps.png. scripts/rendering/run-sustained-performance.py runs it for 603 s, then check-sustained-performance.py applies a fail-closed gate:
- no callback interval over 25 ms
- rolling 10 s windows at or above 59.8 fps
- live counter at or above 59 FPS
- at least 1000 m driven
- quality manifest of MSAA 2 and shadow maps [2048,4096]
- GPU p99 at most 12.5 ms and max below 16.667 ms, from encoder-busy evidence

presentationVerified is always false. GPU diagnostics:
- LoadedGPUProbe: the frozen scene is encoded into an owned MTLCommandBuffer, ABBA variants are created by editing shader-modifier strings, and timing uses gpuStart/EndTime.
- BenchmarkGPUCapture: MTLCaptureManager .gputrace.
- AOPreparationProbe.
- Metal HUD logs.
- An Instruments Game Performance Overview with a CAMetalLayer presentation-calibration app.

The only target is an M2 MacBook Air with 24 GB (rules section 9), where the 10-minute gate currently FAILS (best mean 56.4 fps). Core logic is checked by the SimulationChecks executable: 39 test calls in a custom @main runner, no XCTest. CI (.github/workflows/verify.yml) runs only on ubuntu-24.04 and runs only the Python unit tests for the perf gate and Metal report parser. It never builds Swift, runs SimulationChecks or launches the simulator, and there is no macOS runner. docs/simulator-agent-rules.md is the user's standing contract: accept visuals by inspecting captures against references, preserve the race track scene, and commit and push with Entire-Checkpoint trailers verified on the remote.

fidelity_spec.parameters: argv: '<flag> <outputDir>'. 29 flags recognised in smokeDirectory: --mesh-reuse-test, --shadow-culling-test, --ground-performance-test, --passage-smoke-test, --navigation-smoke-test, --dune-contact-test, --entrance-smoke-test, --viewport-smoke-test, --audio-smoke-test, --weather-reset-test, --storm-race-test, --people-smoke-test, --visual-regression-test, --dust-visibility-test, --sandstorm-smoke-test, --binary-sky-smoke-test, --debris-smoke-test, --loading-smoke-test, --postrace-smoke-test, --trail-material-smoke-test, --town-departure-movie, --smoke-test, --menu-smoke-test, --character-smoke-test, --bb8-motion-smoke-test, --town-smoke-test, --city-escape-smoke-test, --town-benchmark, --renderer-study. Separate: --display-link-lifecycle-check DIR (normal clock). Exit code 0 = pass, 1 = fail. JSON reports use prettyPrinted + sortedKeys. weatherOverride=false (clear) unless the test sets it. Fixed step 1/60 s; raceDelta = step; advancing ignores focus/occlusion. Dispatch at the 20th menu frame; the composite smoke runs at smokeFrames==150 after W held frames 30-89 and D frames 90-119. Smoke runs do not create RaceAudio (except benchmark/audio tests). Scores go to DIR/test-scores.json.

Menu checks (below), then:
- boost+steer with Shift for 4 key pairs (throttle 1, |turn| 1, heading change < -0.04 rad over 0.2 s)
- pause freezes elapsed; Space brake gives speed 0; focus clears held keys; Q/E/R/F head yaw<0 and pitch>0
- reset gives z == -2.6, distance 0, yaw 0
- camera level check for 3 modes x yaws [-2.8,-1,0,1,2.8], pitch 0.7 (|right.y|<1e-5, up.y>0)
- light/dark icon; Marvin tread shoe[7] direction for 4 inputs; model scale 0.60/1.08 within 1e-6; root.y==0; TrackLoop.sample(straight/2).y == 0.0055
- neck concentric at yaw -80/0/80 deg (pivot (0,0.295,-0.01886) within 1e-6) with neck-pan-{-80,0,80}.png
- 5 beacons + labels positioned within 1e-5, label height 0.36, grooves depth FloorGroove.depth
- dirt start: countdown 3, intro camera y=38, mid-intro 3<y<38
- R2-D2: wheels forward>0, brake holds, reverse<0, reset==0 at radius, center/outer tire width ratio 0.75, triangleCount == 25158, 3 wheels, center leg
- BB-8/WALL-E checkMotion; heights 0.67/1.08 and 1.016/1.08 within 1e-7
- racers held during countdown/inactive; 240 frames boosted autopilot: no trail marks while airborne, opponents distance>10 and elapsed>3.9
- brick walls: exactly 2 nodes named '*irregular brick track wall'; 0.5 m vertex grid within 0.3 m of samples at fenceOffset +/- thickness/2; no floating, shortfall <=0.03 m, covered >=90%
- effects frozen at dt=0; trailCounts all >40, racer particles >20; coating >0.5 after 1800 frames
- scores: top 10 persisted
- full 3-lap trail race (TrailRaceSmoke)

inventories.portable_logic:
Reusable without change, or nearly:
- SimulationCore: 20 files, 2,333 lines. Pure Swift with Foundation plus simd, and no AppKit/SceneKit. It needs a small simd shim on Windows (simd_dot/length/distance/normalize/length_squared/cross, simd_quatd, simd_double3x3), and Foundation's FileManager/JSONEncoder for scores.
- SimulationChecks: 15 files, 1,671 lines. Same simd dependency. Its custom runner already avoids XCTest and calls exit(1), so it can run under Swift on Windows or be translated mechanically.
- RaceVoiceChecks.swift: 52 lines, imports only simd.
- Python gates and parsers in scripts/rendering (about 1,380 lines). check-sustained-performance.py (105) and its 27 tests (113), analyze-frame-timeline.py (20), compare-ao-exports.py, check-gtao-fixture.py, check-neutral-ao.py and the test files work on JSON, PNG or KTX only, so they are OS-neutral if the Windows build emits the same benchmark.json, timeline.json and displayed-fps.json schema.
- Apple-specific parsers: read-metal-report.py, profile-metal-timeline.py, summarize-metal-hud.py, read-game-overview.py and check-presentation-calibration.py parse Apple formats and need Windows siblings that emit PresentMon or PIX data in the same JSON shape.
- test-simulator-launch.py (97 lines) and prepare-simulator-assets.py are portable Python. launch-marvin.py drives the macOS build.

Reusable as specification:
- The native smoke and probe code totals about 4,132 lines across Smoke/Checks/Probe/Benchmark/MeshReuse/AOMaterialBinding/TownDepartureMovie/RendererStudy, plus 372 lines of composite smoke in App.swift:787-1158.
- The code is fused to SceneKit/AppKit calls, but the scenario scripts are platform-neutral data that can be lifted into a shared scenario table: spawn points, routes, camera eye/target lists, step counts, inputs, thresholds and JSON keys.
- The decision logic is pure arithmetic on simulation state and can be ported verbatim: PostRace sustained-roaming metrics, People stop/visit metrics, Passage camera metrics, CityEscape impact loop (checkTownImpacts uses only SimulationCore types), Entrance access audits, Sandstorm wind ratios, BinarySky daylight sampling, TrailRace buried-mark logic once a raycast is supplied, and the wall-coverage check once mesh vertex access is supplied.
- Image metrics (changed fraction above 5/255, shadow ratio sweep, magenta audit, luminance windows, trail hue/contrast) are simple loops and can move to a shared module or Python.
- MeshReuseValidation's expanded-index attribute comparison is generic once vertex and index buffers are exposed.

inventories.validation_existing:
What CI runs today (.github/workflows/verify.yml, on push and pull_request, all jobs on ubuntu-24.04):
1. simulator-performance-gate runs only `python3 scripts/rendering/test-sustained-performance.py` (27 tests) and `python3 scripts/rendering/test-metal-report.py` (5 tests). These are unit tests of the JSON/HTML gate and parsers using synthetic fixtures.
2. software runs npm check, Postgres and Playwright for the web portal and server, and uploads browser screenshots.
3. firmware runs an ESP-IDF build.

CI does not build the Swift package, run SimulationChecks, run test-simulator-launch.py, launch the simulator, run any smoke, or render anything. There is no macOS runner or GPU. The root README's Verify section covers only npm and Playwright, plus 'CI also builds the firmware'.

All native validation is manual on the M2 MacBook Air by agents following simulator-agent-rules.md section 10:
- build with build-app.sh
- run the relevant --*-test flags and SimulationChecks
- view the PNGs
- for performance changes, run run-sustained-performance.py (603 s clear and storm) with check-sustained-performance.py, optionally Metal HUD, Instruments overview or GPU capture
- obtain an 'independent Astra Ultra' review for image comparisons and audio redesigns
- commit and push with an Entire-Checkpoint trailer

Current status of gates at 1c8bb11:
- The sustained ten-minute 60 FPS gate has never passed (best mean 56.4 fps).
- The AO restoration controls fail.
- presentationVerified is hard-coded false.
- No smoke compares the build against stored reference images; visual parity with references is judged by people.

Proposed Windows reproduction, as inventory input rather than a strategy choice:
(a) Keep the CLI contract: same flags, output directory and exit codes, and identical JSON key schemas (benchmark.json, timeline.json, displayed-fps.json and every *-test JSON). The existing Python gates, docs and agent rules then keep working.
(b) Add a test-host abstraction with:
- logical input injection
- frame capture of the composited backbuffer, plus offscreen render-to-target at a requested size and MSAA count
- render-mesh raycast, projectPoint and frustum queries
- an offline audio render that writes WAV
- frame-callback and present timestamps
The harness must wait for frames after camera moves, because engines pipeline rendering, and must be able to run long simulations without rendering.
(c) Visual parity between macOS and Windows: before porting, freeze a macOS golden set at commit 1c8bb11. Use deterministic state (weatherOverride, fixed BinaryDaylight fraction and phase, fixed grid and seeds) and all camera lists already encoded in the smokes:
- town 13+2 views
- ground-performance 11 views x 3 lighting conditions
- visual-regression 24 poses and 12 close-ups
- entrance districts, venues and alleys
- passage service views
- navigation captures
- dune orbit
- character fronts and dirty shots
Store the set in Git LFS. Render the same list on Windows at 1920x1080 and compare with perceptual metrics: NVIDIA FLIP, SSIM/MS-SSIM, CIEDE2000, per-region masks, histogram and edge maps. Exact 5/255 thresholds will not hold across renderers. Produce side-by-side contact sheets for human and Astra review, as the rules require.
(d) Within-platform regressions: port the existing self-referential A/B checks unchanged (5/255 changed-fraction gates, shadow-ratio sweep, magenta or error-color audit using the engine's error shader color, sun occlusion luminance, trail hue).
(e) Performance:
- Reimplement TownFrameMeter on engine frame callbacks with QueryPerformanceCounter.
- Take presentation evidence from PresentMon/ETW (MsBetweenPresents and MsBetweenDisplayChange). This finally allows presentationVerified to be true.
- Take GPU headroom from D3D12 timestamp queries or PresentMon GPUBusy, mapped to a new metricKind.
- Use PIX or RenderDoc programmatic capture for --benchmark-gpu-capture.
- Use ETW TraceLogging or PIX markers for TownBenchmarkStart/End.
- Use vendor APIs for thermal and clock telemetry.
- Use high-resolution waitable timers or a waitable swapchain for the 60 Hz update driver.
- Name a Windows target machine and fix its refresh rate, VSync, flip model, and overlays such as Game Bar, Discord and GeForce Experience.
(f) Audio: use the chosen engine's non-real-time render mode (miniaudio, FMOD NRT or Wwise offline), keep the dB-stage assertions, and add cross-platform WAV comparison (EBU R128 loudness, per-stage dBFS deltas, spectral distance) alongside listening review.
(g) CI:
- A GitHub windows-latest job that builds and runs SimulationChecks (pure logic), the Python gates, and smokes that need no GPU fidelity under WARP or lavapipe.
- A self-hosted Windows GPU runner for visual parity and performance.
- Optionally a macos-14 or later job that produces the reference captures.
- Upload artifacts, as the existing browser-evidence step already does.
risks: No golden reference images exist. 'Same graphics' has no objective baseline until a macOS capture set is frozen from commit 1c8bb11. Without one, any Windows result can only be judged by eye, which is the method the rules say failed repeatedly.

Many smoke thresholds are calibrated to SceneKit's exact output. Examples: Marvin opaque body region x550-1000/y250-430 at 1440x900 with luma <0.5 and >1500 samples; magenta r>0.9,b>0.9,g<0.15; sun luminance >0.6/<0.05; trail ratio <0.98 with spread <=0.04; changed fractions <0.001/<0.00001 at 5/255. A new renderer will fail them for benign reasons, and loosening them risks hiding real regressions. The rules forbid 'assertions that merely mirror the implementation' but also forbid silently widening tolerances (check-neutral-ao.py).

The harness assumes SceneKit's synchronous, single-threaded scene mutation followed by immediate snapshot. Engines (Unity, Unreal, Godot) pipeline frames and stream assets, so the harness must be restructured. Long offline simulations (up to 108,000 steps) must run without per-frame rendering.

The frozen GPU probe, AO binding and diagnostic variants rely on SceneKit shader-modifier text surgery and owned-command-buffer rendering. They are not portable and would need to be re-designed or dropped.

The performance gate is hard-coded to Apple semantics and this machine. Examples: quality manifest msaaSamples 2 with shadowMapWidths [2048,4096]; metricKind 'encoderBusyUnion'; allowed flags; 960x540pt x2 = 1080p; 60 Hz cadence. It currently fails on the M2. The rules name the M2 as the sole target, so the Windows performance bar is undefined.

Windows timer granularity (15.6 ms default), DWM composition, VRR, 120/144 Hz panels, MPO and fullscreen optimizations, plus overlay software, can make the 25 ms gap, 59.8 Hz rolling-rate and live-counter >=59 FPS checks fail for reasons unrelated to rendering cost. Activity Monitor was shown to cause stalls on macOS, and Windows has analogous background tools.
DPI scaling: benchmark identity relies on Retina 2x backing. At 125% or 150% DPI on Windows, the same logical window yields a different drawable unless the swapchain size is forced.

Cross-platform floating-point differences (libm sin/cos/atan2, FMA contraction on arm64 vs x64, UCRT) can change long fixed-step replays: 30-minute post-race roaming, storm grids and dune deformation. Smokes that compare against path-dependent outcomes (e.g. 'BB8 ESCAPED', minute-by-minute visibility) may diverge, even though each is self-consistent on its own platform.

Audio thresholds depend on AVAudioEngine DSP details: varispeed latency of 48 samples and pan/volume ramp differences already broke equivalence on macOS. Porting the mixer will shift the dB stage measurements, and the rules require listening comparison in addition to the signal checks.

HUD and overlay captures use AppKit and SF fonts. A Windows HUD will look different (font licensing) and is captured differently, which affects the dirt-hud, race-finish, overlay-storm, fps-overlay and loading checks.

Evidence outside the repo (/Users/thomi/Projects/marvin-town-planning/...) holds the raw timelines and images behind the documented decisions. A Windows team cannot re-inspect them, and only JSON summaries are committed.

CI currently guards none of the simulator. A port could regress SimulationCore or smokes unnoticed unless new CI jobs are added. GitHub-hosted Windows runners have no GPU, so visual and performance validation needs self-hosted hardware.

Process requirements are environment-specific: Entire-Checkpoint trailers verified on the remote, Entire CLI and hooks, and an 'independent Codex Astra Ultra judge'. Their availability on a Windows development machine is unknown, and the rules say not to fabricate checkpoints.

The agent rules and README are macOS-specific: binary path, build-app.sh, 'Apple rendering and frame pacing' section 9, 'Investigate Apple's recommended 3D/game frameworks'. Leaving them unchanged would give contradictory instructions, and the guide itself says to update it when requirements change.

Some docs are stale relative to the code. README says a 2048² sun shadow map (code uses 4096+2048 for two suns). Renderer-study says 29 SimulationChecks (now 39). dirt-city.md mentions 4x MSAA controls (race uses 2x). A port spec built from the docs instead of the code would be wrong.
open_questions: What Windows hardware is the performance target: GPU, CPU, display resolution and refresh rate? Is the bar still 60 FPS at 1920x1080 sustained for 10 minutes in clear and storm, with GPU p99 at most 12.5 ms? The macOS build does not pass that gate today.

Should the macOS SceneKit build at 1c8bb11 be frozen as the golden reference for 'same graphics'? If so, which perceptual metric and tolerance count as parity, and who signs off: the user, the Astra judge, or both?

Must the Windows build keep the identical CLI flags, environment variables and JSON report schemas, so that check-sustained-performance.py, the docs and simulator-agent-rules.md section 10 still apply?

Will the macOS build stay maintained alongside the Windows build, with a shared core and shared tests, and should CI cover both platforms? Is a self-hosted GPU runner (Windows and/or macOS) available?
Is keeping SimulationCore and SimulationChecks in Swift (Swift for Windows plus a simd shim) acceptable, or does the chosen engine require translating the core logic and its 39 checks?

Which diagnostic tools must be ported: the frozen ABBA GPU probe, AO preparation and neutral-binding probes, renderer study and presentation calibration? Or are they macOS-only investigation artifacts?
Should presentation evidence on Windows (PresentMon/ETW) become part of the gate, making presentationVerified true? What GPU metric replaces 'encoderBusyUnion'?
Where should raw validation evidence live for a Windows team? It currently sits in an external directory on one Mac and is not in the repo or LFS.
Do Entire provenance (Entire-Checkpoint trailers, Entire CLI, hooks) and the 'independent Codex Astra Ultra judge' review workflow apply unchanged to Windows port work, and are they available there?
Who updates docs/simulator-agent-rules.md for Windows? Section 9 'Apple rendering and frame pacing' and the macOS entry-point table would need Windows equivalents or explicit scoping.
How should audio parity be accepted: per-stage dBFS deltas, a loudness tolerance between platforms, or a fresh listening comparison per the rules?

Are open, failing items (sustained 60 FPS, AO restoration, intermittent hitches) in scope for the port? Or is the target simply to match current macOS behaviour, including its current performance profile?

missed_fidelity_features.feature: SceneKit shader-stage ordering: lighting and distance fog are applied BEFORE the .fragment entry point, and .surface runs before lighting. Fragment modifiers that assign _output.color replace the lit and fogged result; modifiers that multiply it act on the fogged colour.
missed_fidelity_features.parameters: The sky dome deliberately bypasses fog by assigning _output.color in .fragment (comment 'infinitely distant sky: bypass scene distance fog'). Without this the 220 m dome would be heavily fogged with clear fog 115-240 m and fully fog-coloured with storm fog 3-65 m. CityExitWorld red-soil overlay: '#pragma transparent; _output.color.rgb *= float(in.redSoil); _output.color.a = float(in.redSoil)' multiplies the fogged colour. 11 '#pragma transparent' modifiers rely on the same ordering. Uses linear fog (fogDensityExponent unset, default 1). A port must place its fog in the lit shader and expose a post-fog hook, or the sky and overlays change.
missed_fidelity_features.where: BinarySky.swift:53-90 (fog bypass :89-90), 174, 180; CityExitWorld.swift:83; World.swift:16 (sandbox fog 15-38 m, 0xdbe4df)

missed_fidelity_features.feature: .geometry shader-modifier deformation also runs in the SHADOW-MAP (and depth/normal pre-)passes, so animated and displaced casters cast deformed shadows.

missed_fidelity_features.parameters: AppKit/CoreText draws HUD text at Retina backing scale (2x, e.g. 960x540 pt to 1920x1080 px) with grayscale antialiasing (no subpixel AA on current macOS). Sign plates are rasterised once into NSBitmapImageRep textures with kerning (.kern:tracking), centred paragraphs, .byClipping, and an auto-fit loop that shrinks the font while size>8. The plates are then mip-mapped (mipFilter .linear, maxAnisotropy 8) with emission intensity 0.12. Glyph metrics therefore change sign texture layout.

critic.notes:
1. Coverage. Every Swift file in Sources (70 app + 20 core) and Tests (15) was listed by at least one reader. The only uncovered Swift files are three rendering-tooling fixtures under scripts/rendering, which I read in full: AOPreparationFixture.swift, GroundTruthAOFixture.swift (adds a CryptoKit dependency) and experimental/GroundTruthAO.swift (a rejected Metal-compute GTAO kept as a regression reference; MIT XeGTAO-derived, so it maps directly to HLSL). scripts/city/human-source.blend (25 MB Blender source for the crowd export) was not inspected by anyone. The 30+ .ts scripts in /Users/m1/marvin/scripts belong to the portal and the device 'DeviceSimulator', not this game.

2. Scope reducers worth stating for the design phase. The game uses no SceneKit animation system, particles, physics, morphers, skinners, SpriteKit or scene-file loading. All motion is per-tick code. Particles are CPU-built per-frame geometry. Skinning is a GPU .geometry modifier (CitizenMotion). Physics is pure Swift in SimulationCore. Meshes are procedural or come from custom binary/JSON (Marvin geometry.bin + manifest.json, R2D2 mesh.json, BB8/WallE Generated/mesh.json, City crowd.json). There is no gamepad (GameController/IOKit) support, so parity needs keyboard and mouse only. SCNTransaction is used only to disable implicit actions during world build (App.swift:500-529).

3. Production vs study. Resources/City/sky.hdr is loaded ONLY by the RealityKit RendererStudy (RendererStudy.swift:53-56). Production IBL is the procedural 64x32 8-bit sky probe (BinarySky.swift:184-193; lower hemisphere x0.55; intensity 0.95-0.20*day clear, 0.75 storm). Orthographic cameras appear only in smokes/diagnostics (EntranceSmoke, NavigationSmoke, TrailMaterialSmoke, DirtWorld.swift:726 clod check), and ShadowVolume.swift:20 disables shadow culling for them. SCNLevelOfDetail(screenSpaceRadius:) appears only in LOD-copy helpers (TownShadowBatch.swift:123 is production, but all production LODs are worldSpaceDistance). MTLDevice.supportsFamily(.apple1) chooses .shared vs .managed storage for the sand and coating textures (DeformableSand.swift:125, DirtCoating.swift:71).

4. Correction to the app-shell reader. Avenir Next Condensed appears only in TownSigns.swift:46. MainMenu and LevelLoading use NSFont.systemFont/monospacedDigitSystemFont.

5. Portability facts. SimulationCore depends only on Foundation (FileManager plus JSON in DirtRace.swift:294-314) and the simd module (86 call sites incl. simd_quatd and simd_double3x3), so a small simd shim makes it compile with Swift on Windows. Tests use only Foundation and simd (25 simd calls). String(format:) with %@ (TownSmoke, PeopleSmoke and others) and JSONSerialization .sortedKeys exist in swift-corelibs-foundation, but output formatting should be checked. Where UserDefaults and .applicationSupportDirectory land on Windows under corelibs-foundation must be verified.

6. Validation infrastructure. CI (/Users/m1/marvin/.github/workflows/verify.yml) runs on ubuntu-24.04 only and never builds Swift or runs SimulationChecks or smokes. The simulator job runs only test-sustained-performance.py and test-metal-report.py, so all simulator validation today is local and macOS-only. A Windows port needs its own CI runner for the SimulationChecks executable and a headless offscreen-render path to replace the 15 SCNRenderer.snapshot smokes.

7. Asset footprint (du). Resources total 170 MB: Audio 49M (161 WAV plus CREDITS.md and Credits.rtf), City 44M, WallE 42M, Marvin 16M, R2D2 11M, BB8 6.6M, Dirt 2.1M, Icons 428K. Branch codex/mos-aster-racing-city at 1c8bb11.

8. Items flagged 'verify'. The specific SCNCamera and SCNLight default values above come from Apple's documented defaults and should be confirmed with a runtime property dump before the port, because the code never sets them. The same applies to which lighting terms SceneKit SSAO attenuates. Nothing was built or launched.
